d: A bold buffalo ranch chicken sandwich that brings the heat of classic buffalo wings to a fried chicken sandwich. Crispy fried chicken breast is tossed in tangy Frank's RedHot buffalo sauce, then layered with a cool homemade ranch drizzle, buffalo ranch slaw with red onions and celery, a sweet-spicy buffalo bacon jam, and a creamy buffalo ranch cream cheese spread. Finished with candied jalapeños, fried green tomato, and onion rings for the ultimate buffalo experience.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
1 tablespoon Frank's RedHot sauce (for wet batter)
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
1 fried green tomato slice (or fried red tomato slice)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and 1 tablespoon Frank's RedHot sauce.
In another shallow bowl, combine flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, salt, and black pepper.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes, then toss in buffalo sauce.
In a small saucepan over medium-low heat, melt the butter.
Add Frank's RedHot sauce, Worcestershire sauce, and garlic powder.
Whisk until combined and warmed through, about 2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Toss the fried chicken in the sauce to coat.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, buttermilk, and sour cream until smooth.
Stir in chives, dill, parsley, minced garlic, and lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate until ready to use.
In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage, carrots, red onions, and celery.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, Frank's RedHot, apple cider vinegar, and ranch seasoning.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook the diced bacon until crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove half the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in Frank's RedHot sauce, brown sugar, and apple cider vinegar.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Season with salt. Let cool slightly — it will thicken as it cools.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese, Frank's RedHot, ranch seasoning, and garlic powder.
Mix until smooth and well blended.
Stir in minced chives. Season with salt.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread Buffalo Ranch Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Spoon a generous layer of Buffalo Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Place the buffalo sauce-tossed chicken on top.
Drizzle Homemade Ranch Dressing over the chicken.
Pile on Buffalo Ranch Slaw.
Add candied jalapeños, fried green tomato, and onion rings.
Place the top bun and serve immediately.

t: Buffalo Cream Cheese Dip Chicken Sandwich

Place the fried chicken on top.
Drizzle Buffalo Cream Cheese Drizzle over the chicken.

Place the top bun and serve immediately.

A fresh citrus-forward slaw, a sweet-spicy honey-bacon jam, and a smooth goat cheese spread create layers of flavor. Finished with crispy bacon, pickled red onions, and fresh herbs for a balanced, sophisticated take on the viral sensation.

Pile on Hot Honey Slaw.
Add crispy bacon strips and pickled red onions.
Place the top bun and serve immediately while the chicken and honey are still warm.

t: Smokey Dr Pepper BBQ Chicken Sandwich
d: The secret ingredient is soda. A full can of Dr Pepper gets reduced down with tomato sauce, brown sugar, smoked paprika, and liquid smoke into a thick, sticky, cherry-caramel BBQ glaze that coats crispy fried chicken. Topped with melty pepper jack, maple bacon bourbon jam, and fried onion rings, this is BBQ done different.
i: 2-3 cups (enough for 350°F deep frying) Beef tallow or lard for frying
1 can (12 oz) Dr Pepper (regular, not diet)
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Smokey Dr Pepper Goat Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
Smokey Dr Pepper BBQ Sauce (on chicken)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a medium saucepan, combine Dr Pepper, tomato sauce, and brown sugar.
Add apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and reduces by about one-third.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly. Toss the fried chicken in the sauce to coat.
In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage, carrots, and red onions.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, sugar, and celery seed.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook the diced bacon until crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove half the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add diced onion and cook until softened and golden, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the bourbon and let simmer for 2-3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Add the Dr Pepper BBQ sauce and brown sugar.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Season with salt. Let cool slightly—it will thicken as it cools.
In a small bowl, combine softened goat cheese with 2 tablespoons of the cooled Dr Pepper BBQ sauce.
Mix until smooth and well blended.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread Smokey Dr Pepper Goat Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Spoon a generous layer of Smokey Dr Pepper Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Place the BBQ sauce-coated chicken on top.
Pile on Dr Pepper BBQ Slaw.
Top with melted pepper jack cheese and fried onion rings.
Place the top bun and serve immediately.

t: Maple Bourbon Bacon BBQ Chicken Sandwich
d: An elevated take on BBQ chicken that combines sweet maple syrup, bourbon, and smoky bacon with a rich maple-bourbon glaze. Topped with candied bacon strips, crispy fried egg for richness and creaminess, plus aged Gruyère for a sophisticated yet indulgent sandwich that's pure elevated comfort food.
i: 2-3 cups (enough for 350°F deep frying) Beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Maple Bourbon Peach Chutney Goat Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a medium saucepan, combine maple syrup, bourbon, and BBQ sauce.
Add brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to medium.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and reduces slightly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly. Toss the fried chicken in the sauce to coat.
Preheat oven to 375°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, combine maple syrup and brown sugar.
Lay thick-cut bacon strips on the baking sheet.
Brush or drizzle the maple mixture evenly over the bacon.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until the bacon is crispy and caramelized.
Remove from oven and let cool on a paper towel to crisp up further.
In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage, carrots, and red onions.
In a small bowl, whisk together apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, and salt.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with black pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a small bowl, combine softened aged cheddar with 1-2 tablespoons of the cooled maple bourbon sauce.
Mix until smooth and well blended.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread Aged Cheddar Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the bourbon-maple coated chicken on top.
Pile on Maple Bourbon Slaw.
Top with candied bacon strips and crispy onion rings.
Place the top bun and serve immediately.

t: Alabama White BBQ Sauce Chicken Sandwich
d: A distinctive departure from traditional red BBQ, this creamy Alabama white sauce celebrates the legendary Big Bob Gibson tradition. Made with a mayo and horseradish base with apple cider vinegar and lemon brightness, it's topped with smoked Gouda, tangy vinegar coleslaw with crispy bacon, and dill pickles for a uniquely Southern experience.
i: 2-3 cups (enough for 350°F deep frying) Beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Alabama White BBQ Goat Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.

In a bowl, combine mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, and yellow mustard.

Add fresh lemon juice and a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Whisk until smooth and well combined.
Let sit for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Drizzle over the fried chicken before assembly.

In a small bowl, whisk together apple cider vinegar, fresh lemon juice, a touch of honey or sugar, and salt.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with black pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, mustard seeds, sugar, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then remove from heat.
Add thinly sliced red onions and sliced jalapeños to a jar.
Pour the hot pickling liquid over the vegetables.
Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese with 1 tablespoon of the cooled Alabama white sauce.
Mix until smooth and well blended.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread White Sauce Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Drizzle Alabama White BBQ Sauce over the chicken.
Place the white sauce-coated chicken on top.
Pile on White BBQ Slaw.
Add White BBQ Pickled Vegetables and fresh tomato slices.
Place the top bun and serve immediately.

d: Inspired by the iconic Burger King Rodeo sandwich, this creative combination balances sweet BBQ sauce with cool, creamy ranch dressing. Crispy onion rings add textural contrast, while sharp cheddar and crispy shallots elevate this indulgent sandwich with textural sophistication and gourmet fried chicken technique.
i: 2-3 cups (enough for 350°F deep frying) Beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
BBQ Ranch Goat Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a small saucepan, combine ketchup, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce.
Add garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, and a pinch of cayenne pepper.
Whisk until combined over medium heat.
Warm through for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove from heat. Set aside for assembly.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, buttermilk, and sour cream until smooth.
Stir in minced fresh chives, dill, and parsley.
Add minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, salt, and black pepper.
Mix well and refrigerate until ready to use.
In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage, carrots, and red onions.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, a touch of BBQ sauce, ranch seasoning, and salt.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with black pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a small bowl, combine softened American cheese with 1 tablespoon BBQ sauce and 1/2 teaspoon ranch seasoning.
Mix until smooth and well blended.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread BBQ Ranch Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the BBQ sauce-coated chicken on top.
Drizzle ranch dressing over the chicken.
Pile on Rodeo Slaw.
Add crispy onion rings, crispy bacon strips, and melted American cheese.
Place the top bun and serve immediately.

t: Berry Bacon Brie BBQ Chicken Sandwich
d: An elegant, elevated take on BBQ chicken that celebrates sophisticated flavors. Fresh blackberries and raspberries are combined with BBQ sauce and balsamic vinegar for a sweet-tart glaze, topped with crispy bacon, melted brie, fresh arugula, and a balsamic drizzle for a truly gourmet experience with perfect flavor balance.
i: 2-3 cups (enough for 350°F deep frying) Beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Brie Goat Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a small saucepan, combine fresh blackberries, raspberries, and BBQ sauce.
Add balsamic vinegar and brown sugar.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Let simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the berries break down and the sauce thickens slightly.
Strain through a fine sieve if you prefer a smoother sauce, or leave berry pulp in for texture.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove from heat. Drizzle over the fried chicken before assembly.
In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage, carrots, and thinly sliced red onions.
In a small bowl, whisk together balsamic vinegar, a touch of raspberry vinegar if available, honey, and Dijon mustard.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook thick-cut bacon strips until crispy, about 8-10 minutes.
Transfer to a paper towel to drain and cool slightly.
Keep warm until ready to assemble.
Butter both halves of the brioche bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Place softened brie cheese on the bottom bun—it will warm slightly from the hot bun.
Place the berry-BBQ coated chicken on top.
Pile on Berry BBQ Slaw.
Add crispy bacon strips, fresh arugula, and a few fresh berries for garnish.
Place the top bun and serve immediately.

t: Texas Pepper Spicy and Sweet BBQ Chicken Sandwich
d: A bold, peppery Texas-style BBQ sandwich featuring Dave's Devil Spit BBQ Sauce, hellfire spicy sweet pickles, and candied peppered pork belly. Smoky heat meets sweet and tangy with pickled cherry peppers and sweet corn relish.
i: for frying Beef tallow or lard
1 tbsp Dave's Gourmet Insanity Sauce or similar devil/ghost pepper hot sauce
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Texas Pepper Bacon Jam (on bottom bun)
Texas Pepper Goat Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
Dave's Devil Spit BBQ Sauce (on chicken)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, cayenne pepper, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a medium saucepan, combine BBQ sauce, brown sugar, and apple cider vinegar.
Finely mince fresh jalapeños and habaneros (seeds included for maximum heat).
Add minced peppers to the sauce along with a pinch of ghost pepper powder for serious heat.
Add smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and cumin.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Let simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and pepper flavors meld.
Season with salt to taste.
Remove from heat. Drizzle over the fried chicken before assembly.
Slice onions into rings and separate the layers.
In a shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, cornstarch, cayenne pepper, jalapeño powder, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
In another shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
Dip onion rings in wet batter, then dredge in the spicy dry mixture.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F.
Fry the onion rings in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Transfer to a paper towel and season with salt while warm.
In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage, carrots, and red onions.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, buttermilk, fresh lime juice, and ranch seasoning.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a small bowl, combine softened pepper jack cheese with 1 tablespoon of the cooled Texas pepper BBQ sauce.
Mix until smooth and well blended.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread Pepper Jack Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the spicy pepper-coated chicken on top.
Pile on Texas Pepper Slaw.
Top with pepper fried onion rings and melted pepper jack cheese.
Add sliced fresh jalapeños if you want even more heat.
Place the top bun and serve immediately with cooling beverages nearby.

d: This sandwich combines the classic Japanese teriyaki glaze with sweet grilled pineapple and bright pickled ginger. The umami-rich teriyaki coating on the crispy fried chicken breast is balanced by tropical fruit and the gentle heat of fresh ginger, creating a perfect East-meets-island fusion. Pineapple and jalapeño bacon jam adds a spicy-sweet layer that complements the savory teriyaki perfectly.
i: 2 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Pineapple Jalapeño Bacon Jam (on bottom bun)
Teriyaki Pineapple Goat Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and 2 tablespoons mirin.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, salt, and white pepper.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep skillet or Dutch oven.
Dredge the chicken breast in the flour mixture, coating both sides evenly.
Dip the floured chicken into the wet batter, shaking off excess.
Carefully place the chicken into the hot fat and fry for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
In a small saucepan over medium heat, combine soy sauce, mirin, and sake.
Add brown sugar, minced ginger, and minced garlic.
Simmer for 4-5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and becomes glossy.
Remove from heat and set aside.
Cook chopped bacon in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium heat until crispy (6-7 minutes).
Remove bacon and set aside, leaving 2 tablespoons bacon fat in the skillet.
Add diced onion and jalapeño to the fat and sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Return bacon to the skillet and add diced pineapple and sugar.
Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture becomes jam-like and caramelized.
Remove from heat and cool slightly.
In a medium bowl, combine shredded cabbage, carrots, and red onions.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, sugar, and celery seed.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Add sesame oil and season with salt and black pepper to taste.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese and fresh goat cheese until smooth.
Fold in pineapple juice and garlic powder.
Season with salt to taste.
Butter the cut sides of a yellow potato or brioche bun and toast until golden.
Spread the Teriyaki Pineapple Goat Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Add a thin layer of Pineapple Jalapeño Bacon Jam.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.
Brush the chicken with warm Teriyaki Sauce.
Pile the Teriyaki Pineapple Slaw on the chicken.
Add the top bun and serve immediately while warm.

d: Inspired by the beloved Chinese-American takeout classic, this sandwich features crispy fried chicken breast glazed in a sweet and tangy orange sauce infused with ginger and garlic. The bright citrus notes are balanced by the savory umami of soy sauce and a hint of heat from red pepper flakes. Pickled red onions and fresh cilantro add brightness and complexity, while a cool red cabbage slaw provides textural contrast to the sticky glaze.

2 tbsp ground pork, cooked and crumbled
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Crab Rangoon Cream Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, orange zest, minced ginger, salt, and white pepper.

Dip the floured chicken into the wet batter, shaking off excess.
Carefully place the chicken into the hot fat and fry for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
In a small saucepan over medium heat, combine fresh orange juice, orange zest, soy sauce, and ginger.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes.
Simmer for 4-5 minutes until the sauce begins to thicken.
Add brown sugar and stir until dissolved.
Simmer for an additional 2-3 minutes until glossy. Remove from heat.
In a medium bowl, combine shredded red cabbage, carrots, and pickled red onions.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, rice vinegar, sugar, and sesame oil.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Thinly slice red onions and place in a small jar.
In a small saucepan, heat rice vinegar and sugar over medium heat until sugar dissolves.
Pour the warm vinegar mixture over the onions.
Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until ready to use (at least 30 minutes).
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese with fresh orange juice and zest.
Stir in minced garlic and salt to taste.
Butter the cut sides of a yellow potato or brioche bun and toast until golden.
Spread the Orange Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.
Brush the chicken with warm Orange Sauce.
Pile the Red Cabbage Slaw on the chicken.
Add any additional pickled red onions on top.
Top with the bun and serve immediately.

d: A celebration of Asian sesame flavors, this sandwich features crispy fried chicken breast coated with toasted sesame seeds and finished with a nutty sesame-soy glaze. Layers of shredded red cabbage, pickled ginger, cucumber, and a silky sesame-ginger cream cheese spread create a delicate balance of textures and flavors. This refined sandwich honors traditional Asian cuisine while delivering the satisfying crunch of fried chicken.

1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Crab Rangoon Cream Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.

Press toasted sesame seeds onto both sides of the wet battered chicken.
Carefully place the chicken into the hot fat and fry for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
In a small bowl, whisk together sesame oil, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and minced garlic.
Stir in toasted sesame seeds.
Set aside until ready to use.
In a medium bowl, combine shredded red cabbage, julienned cucumber, and sliced scallions.
In a small bowl, whisk together sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, and sesame salt.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Let sit for 5 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.
Butter the cut sides of a yellow potato or brioche bun and toast until golden.
Spread the Sesame-Ginger Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.
Drizzle with Sesame-Soy Glaze.
Pile the Red Cabbage & Cucumber Slaw on the chicken.
Add a layer of pickled ginger slices.
Top with the bun and serve immediately.

The heat is mellowed by a cool red cabbage and carrot slaw, while a spicy mayo and cilantro finish add fresh herbaceous notes that balance the intense spice.

1/2 tablespoon Szechuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
2 dried red chilies, deseeded and minced

1/2 tsp Szechuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Crispy Chili Oil Bacon Jam (on bottom bun)
Crab Rangoon Cream Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.

In a small saucepan over low heat, warm chili oil.
Add Szechuan peppercorns, minced ginger, and minced garlic.
Cook gently for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add soy sauce and brown sugar.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, combine shredded red cabbage and carrots.
In a small bowl, whisk together sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, and sesame salt.

Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, chili oil, minced garlic, and crushed Szechuan peppercorns.
Fold in fresh minced cilantro.
Season with salt to taste.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese with chili oil.
Stir in minced garlic and a pinch of Szechuan peppercorns.
Season with salt to taste.
Butter the cut sides of a yellow potato or brioche bun and toast until golden.
Spread the Szechuan Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.
Brush generously with warm Szechuan Chili Glaze.
Pile the Red Cabbage & Carrot Slaw on the chicken.

d: A reimagining of Korean BBQ in sandwich form, this dish features crispy fried chicken breast glazed with a sweet, savory, and slightly spicy gochujang-soy sauce. Grilled kimchi and caramelized onions add umami depth, while cool pickled cucumber and fresh scallions provide brightness. A silky gochujang cream cheese spread ties everything together with bold Korean flavors that build with each bite.
i: 2 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Korean BBQ Bacon Jam (on bottom bun)
Crab Rangoon Cream Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.

Whisk until smooth and simmer for 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat and set aside.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and lightly butter.
Add kimchi (drained if very wet) and cook for 2-3 minutes until warmed through and edges begin to brown slightly.
Remove from heat and set aside.
Thinly slice onions.
In a large skillet over medium-low heat, melt 1 tablespoon butter.
Add onions and a pinch of salt.
Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until onions are deeply browned and sweet.
Set aside.

Spread gochujang cream cheese on the bottom bun.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.
Brush with warm Korean BBQ Glaze.
Layer the grilled kimchi on the chicken.
Top with caramelized onions.
Add fresh scallions and pickled cucumber slices.
Top with the bun and serve immediately.

d: A fiery Korean take on the classic fried chicken sandwich, featuring crispy fried chicken breast coated with a spicy gochujang crust. The sandwich layers bold gochujang mayo, crispy fried shallots, pickled daikon radish, and cool red cabbage slaw to create a complex interplay of heat, sweetness, and acid. Crab Rangoon Cream Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)

In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese with creamy peanut butter.

Butter the cut sides of a yellow potato or brioche bun and toast until golden.
Spread the Peanut Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.

In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese with honey.
Add roasted garlic cloves (mashed) or minced fresh garlic.
Stir until smooth and well combined.
Butter the cut sides of a yellow potato or brioche bun and toast until golden.
Spread the Honey Garlic Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.
Brush generously with warm Honey Garlic Glaze.
Pile the Red Cabbage Slaw on the chicken.
Garnish with fresh cilantro, sliced scallions, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.
Top with the bun and serve immediately.

d: A sophisticated Japanese-inspired sandwich that highlights the umami depth of miso paste combined with the warm spice of fresh ginger. Crispy fried chicken breast is glazed with a complex miso-ginger sauce enriched with butter and a touch of sake. Cool red cabbage slaw, pickled ginger, and a creamy miso-ginger spread layer together to create a sandwich that's both comforting and refined, perfect for adventurous palates.
i: 2 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Miso Ginger Bacon Jam (on bottom bun)
Wasabi Crab Rangoon Cream Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and 1 tablespoon white miso paste (dissolved smooth).
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, salt, and white pepper.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep skillet or Dutch oven.
Dredge the chicken breast in the flour mixture, coating both sides evenly.
Dip the floured chicken into the wet batter, shaking off excess.
Carefully place the chicken into the hot fat and fry for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt 2 tablespoons butter.
Add minced fresh ginger and minced garlic, sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Dissolve 2 tablespoons white miso paste in a small amount of sake, then add to the pan.
Add 1/4 cup sake and stir well.
Simmer for 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and becomes glossy.
Remove from heat and set aside.
In a medium bowl, combine shredded red cabbage and carrots.
In a small bowl, whisk together sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, minced ginger, and sesame salt.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Let sit for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese with 1 tablespoon white miso paste.
Add minced fresh ginger and a pinch of garlic powder.
Stir until smooth and well combined.
Butter the cut sides of a yellow potato or brioche bun and toast until golden.
Spread the Miso-Ginger Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.
Brush with warm Miso Ginger Glaze.
Pile the Red Cabbage Slaw on the chicken.
Add a layer of pickled ginger slices.
Garnish with fresh scallions and a pinch of sesame seeds.
Top with the bun and serve immediately.

t: Sushi Sauce Pickled Ginger Chicken Sandwich
d: Inspired by the delicate flavors of sushi, this refined sandwich combines crispy fried chicken breast with a wasabi-spiked sushi sauce and bright pickled ginger. A creamy avocado and cream cheese spread adds richness, while a cool red cabbage slaw provides textural contrast. Fresh cilantro, scallions, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds complete this elegant sandwich that captures the essence of Japanese sushi in a new form.
i: 2 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
2 oz imitation crab meat, finely chopped
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Imitation Crab Seaweed Cream Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, sesame seeds, salt, white pepper, and a pinch of wasabi powder (optional).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep skillet or Dutch oven.
Dredge the chicken breast in the flour mixture, coating both sides evenly.
Dip the floured chicken into the wet batter, shaking off excess.
Carefully place the chicken into the hot fat and fry for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise and soy sauce.
Add rice vinegar and a tiny amount of wasabi powder (start with 1/8 teaspoon and adjust to taste).
Whisk until smooth and well combined.
Set aside until ready to use.
In a medium bowl, combine shredded red cabbage and carrots.
In a small bowl, whisk together sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, and sesame salt.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cut a ripe avocado in half, remove the pit, and scoop into a small bowl.
Mash together with softened cream cheese until smooth.
Add lime juice and salt to taste.
Butter the cut sides of a yellow potato or brioche bun and toast until golden.
Spread the Avocado Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.
Drizzle with Sushi Sauce.
Pile the Red Cabbage Slaw on the chicken.
Add a layer of pickled ginger slices.
Garnish with fresh cilantro, sliced scallions, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.
Top with the bun and serve immediately.

d: This creative sandwich captures the beloved flavors of Chinese egg rolls in a new form. Crispy fried chicken breast is topped with a silky Crab Rangoon Cream Cheese Spread—inspired by the classic Chinese-American appetizer—and paired with a spicy-sweet sauce. A crunchy slaw of red cabbage, carrots, and cucumber provides textural contrast, while crispy fried wonton strips and fresh cilantro add authentic egg roll character to every bite.
i: 2 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Egg Roll Bacon Jam (on bottom bun)
Crab Rangoon Cream Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, salt, white pepper, and a pinch of garlic powder.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep skillet or Dutch oven.
Dredge the chicken breast in the flour mixture, coating both sides evenly.
Dip the floured chicken into the wet batter, shaking off excess.
Carefully place the chicken into the hot fat and fry for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
In a small saucepan over medium heat, combine sweet chili sauce and soy sauce.
Add rice vinegar and minced garlic.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes until blended and glossy.
Remove from heat and set aside.
In a medium bowl, combine shredded red cabbage, carrots, and julienned cucumber.
In a small bowl, whisk together sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, and sesame salt.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese with cooked crab meat (fresh or canned, drained).
Add minced green onions (scallions) and minced garlic.
Stir in a tiny squeeze of soy sauce and salt to taste.
Mix until well combined and spreadable.
Cut wonton wrappers into thin strips (about 1/4-inch wide).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 325°F in a heavy-bottomed skillet.
Carefully add wonton strips in small batches and fry for 1-2 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Season lightly with salt.
Butter the cut sides of a yellow potato or brioche bun and toast until golden.
Spread the Crab Rangoon Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.
Brush with warm Sweet & Spicy Egg Roll Sauce.
Pile the Red Cabbage Slaw on the chicken.
Top with crispy fried wonton strips.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and sliced scallions.
Top with the bun and serve immediately.

d: A bold, contemporary take on Asian sandwich flavors, this dish features crispy fried chicken breast topped with a vibrant, spicy-rich chili crisp mayo infused with garlic and Szechuan peppercorns. Cool red cabbage slaw provides heat-balancing crunch, while fresh cilantro and scallions add brightness. A touch of lime juice brings acidity that ties everything together, creating a modern Asian-inspired sandwich that's complex, fiery, and utterly craveable.
i: 2 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
1.5 tablespoons chili crisp oil (Lao Gan Ma or homemade)
2 tbsp chili crisp oil (Lao Gan Ma)
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Chili Crisp Bacon Jam (on bottom bun)
Crab Rangoon Cream Cheese Spread (on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, salt, white pepper, and a pinch of Szechuan peppercorn powder (optional).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep skillet or Dutch oven.
Dredge the chicken breast in the flour mixture, coating both sides evenly.
Dip the floured chicken into the wet batter, shaking off excess.
Carefully place the chicken into the hot fat and fry for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise with 2-3 tablespoons chili crisp.
Add minced garlic, crushed Szechuan peppercorns, and sesame oil.
Stir until well combined.
Taste and adjust heat level as desired.
In a medium bowl, combine shredded red cabbage, carrots, and sliced scallions.
In a small bowl, whisk together sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, and sesame salt.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese with sesame oil.
Add lime juice (about 1 teaspoon) and minced garlic.
Stir until smooth and well combined.
Butter the cut sides of a yellow potato or brioche bun and toast until golden.
Spread the Lime-Sesame Spread on the bottom bun.
Place the hot fried chicken breast on top.
Generously spread Chili Crisp Mayo over the chicken.
Pile the Red Cabbage Slaw on the chicken.
Garnish with fresh cilantro, additional sliced scallions, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.
Add a final drizzle of additional chili crisp if desired for extra heat.
Top with the bun and serve immediately.

d: A vibrant sandwich that brings the creamy comfort of Indian tikka masala to a crispy fried chicken sandwich. Boneless, skinless chicken breast fried in beef tallow is smothered in a smooth, aromatic tomato-based sauce enriched with cream and perfumed with warming spices like garam masala, turmeric, and coriander. Layered on a buttered and toasted brioche bun with a samosa-style spread of curry basmati rice, mashed peas, and mashed potato, tangy mint-cucumber lassi slaw, and a spiced tikka masala bacon jam. Topped with crispy fried onions, pickled red onions, and fresh cilantro for a perfect balance of rich sauce, crunchy textures, and herbaceous brightness.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
1/2 teaspoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed
1/4 cup frozen peas, thawed and mashed
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
dir: Pat the chicken breast dry with paper towels to ensure a crispy crust.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and whole milk until combined.

In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, garam masala, turmeric, cumin, coriander, cayenne, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly to distribute seasonings evenly.
Dip the chicken breast into the wet batter, coating thoroughly on all sides. Let excess drip off.
Transfer to the dry batter and coat completely, pressing gently so the coating adheres. For extra crispiness, dip back into the wet batter and then into the dry batter a second time.
Heat beef tallow or lard in a heavy-bottomed pot or deep skillet to 350°F. Use a thermometer to maintain consistent temperature.
Carefully place the breaded chicken into the hot oil. Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until the internal temperature reaches 165°F. The coating should be deep golden brown.
Remove the fried chicken with a slotted spoon and place on a wire rack (not paper towels) to cool slightly and maintain crispiness.
Heat 2 tablespoons butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add 1/4 teaspoon cumin seeds and toast for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add 1/3 cup diced yellow onion and cook for 6-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion is golden and softened.
Add 1 tablespoon minced ginger and 3 minced garlic cloves; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 1/2 teaspoon turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon cumin powder, 1/2 teaspoon coriander powder, and 1 teaspoon garam masala; stir constantly for 1 minute.
Add 3/4 cup crushed tomatoes and stir well; simmer for 8-10 minutes over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and carefully pour the mixture into a blender. Blend on high until completely smooth, about 1-2 minutes. (Alternatively, use an immersion blender in the saucepan.)
Pour the blended sauce back into the saucepan and return to medium heat.
Stir in 1/4 cup heavy cream, 1 teaspoon honey, and 1/2 teaspoon crushed dried fenugreek leaves.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Keep warm on low heat.

In a large bowl, combine 1 cup shredded red cabbage, 1/4 cup shredded carrots, 1/4 cup diced cucumber, 2 tablespoons thinly sliced red onions, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh mint, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk together 3 tablespoons plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon lime juice, 1/4 teaspoon cumin powder, and 1 teaspoon sugar.
Pour the yogurt dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Refrigerate until ready to use.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook 4 strips of diced thick-cut bacon until crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove half the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add 1/2 diced yellow onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves and 1 teaspoon minced ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in 1 teaspoon garam masala and 1/2 teaspoon cumin powder; cook for 30 seconds.
Add 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar, and 1 teaspoon tomato paste.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Season with salt to taste. Let cool slightly — it will thicken as it cools.
In a small bowl, combine 2 ounces softened cream cheese and 1 ounce fresh goat cheese; mix until smooth.
Mash 1/4 cup thawed frozen peas lightly with a fork and fold into the cream cheese.
Fold in 3 tablespoons cooked curry basmati rice and 2 tablespoons mashed boiled potato.

Stir in 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1 teaspoon cumin powder, 1/2 teaspoon coriander powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, 1 tablespoon minced cilantro, 1 tablespoon sautéed diced onion, and 1 teaspoon minced green chili.
Season with salt to taste. Mix until well combined.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes per side until golden and fragrant.
Spread the Samosa Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Add a layer of Tikka Masala Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Place the fried chicken on the jam.
Spoon 2-3 tablespoons of warm Tikka Masala Sauce over the chicken.
Pile the Mint Cucumber Lassi Slaw on top of the sauce.
Scatter crispy fried onions and pickled red onions over the slaw.
Sprinkle fresh cilantro over the toppings.
Cap with the toasted top bun.
Serve immediately while the chicken is still warm and the slaw is crisp.

d: An elegant sandwich featuring tender fried chicken breast bathed in a luxurious North Indian-style korma sauce made with coconut cream, ground almonds, and yogurt, infused with warming spices like cinnamon and coriander. The samosa-style spread brings curry basmati rice, mashed peas, and mashed potato into each bite, while the mint-cucumber lassi slaw provides cool, herbaceous relief from the rich sauce. Topped with toasted almond slices for subtle nutty crunch and bright cilantro, all served on a buttered and toasted brioche bun. Every layer—creamy sauce, crunchy almonds, tangy slaw, and spiced spread—works in harmony to create sophisticated comfort food.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
1/4 cup frozen peas, thawed and mashed
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
dir: Pat the chicken breast dry with paper towels to ensure a crispy crust.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and whole milk until combined.

In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, ground cinnamon, coriander, turmeric, white pepper, and salt. Mix thoroughly to distribute seasonings evenly.
Dip the chicken breast into the wet batter, coating thoroughly on all sides. Let excess drip off.
Transfer to the dry batter and coat completely, pressing gently so the coating adheres. For extra crispiness, dip back into the wet batter and then into the dry batter a second time.
Heat beef tallow or lard in a heavy-bottomed pot or deep skillet to 350°F. Use a thermometer to maintain consistent temperature.
Carefully place the breaded chicken into the hot oil. Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until the internal temperature reaches 165°F. The coating should be deep golden brown.
Remove the fried chicken with a slotted spoon and place on a wire rack (not paper towels) to cool slightly and maintain crispiness.
Heat 2 tablespoons ghee or butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add 1/2 thinly sliced yellow onion and cook for 8-9 minutes, stirring frequently, until golden brown and caramelized. This step is important for korma authenticity.
Add 1 teaspoon minced ginger and 2 minced garlic cloves; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 1 broken cinnamon stick piece; cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in 1 teaspoon coriander powder and 1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder; cook for 30 seconds.
Remove from heat and let cool for 1 minute. Whisk in 2 tablespoons plain yogurt slowly, stirring constantly to avoid curdling.
Return to medium-low heat and gently warm through for 1-2 minutes. Do not boil.
Stir in 3 tablespoons coconut cream and 2 tablespoons ground almonds, whisking until smooth.
Add 2 tablespoons chicken stock and simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste. Remove the cinnamon stick piece before serving. Keep warm on low heat.

In a large bowl, combine 1 cup shredded red cabbage, 1/4 cup shredded carrots, 1/4 cup diced cucumber, 2 tablespoons thinly sliced red onions, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh mint, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk together 3 tablespoons plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon lime juice, 1/4 teaspoon cumin powder, and 1 teaspoon sugar.
Pour the yogurt dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Refrigerate until ready to use.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook 4 strips of diced thick-cut bacon until crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove half the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add 1/2 diced yellow onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves and 1 teaspoon minced ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in 1/2 teaspoon coriander powder and cook for 30 seconds.
Add 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar, 1 tablespoon coconut cream, and 1 tablespoon ground almonds.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Season with salt to taste. Let cool slightly — it will thicken as it cools.
In a small bowl, combine 2 ounces softened cream cheese and 1 ounce fresh goat cheese; mix until smooth.
Mash 1/4 cup thawed frozen peas lightly with a fork and fold into the cream cheese.
Fold in 2 tablespoons mashed boiled potato, 3 tablespoons cooked curry basmati rice, and 2 tablespoons sweetened coconut flakes.

Stir in 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1 teaspoon cumin powder, 1/2 teaspoon coriander powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, 1 tablespoon minced cilantro, 1 tablespoon sautéed diced onion, and 1 teaspoon minced green chili.
Season with salt to taste. Mix until well combined.
In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast 2 tablespoons sliced almonds, stirring frequently, for 3-4 minutes until light golden and fragrant.
Remove to a plate and set aside.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes per side until golden and fragrant.
Spread the Samosa Coconut Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Add a layer of Korma Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Place the fried chicken on the jam.
Spoon 2-3 tablespoons of warm Korma Sauce over the chicken.
Scatter toasted almond slices on top of the sauce.
Add a dollop of mango chutney.
Pile some Mint Cucumber Lassi Slaw on top of the chutney.
Sprinkle fresh chopped cilantro over everything.
Cap with the toasted top bun.
Serve immediately while warm.

d: A vibrant Thai-Indian fusion sandwich that marries the best of both culinary traditions with a creamy, aromatic coconut curry sauce infused with warm turmeric, cumin, ginger, and garlic, brightened with fresh lime juice. The fried chicken breast is nestled in a samosa-style spread of curry basmati rice, mashed peas, and mashed potato, then layered with a mango chutney slaw that brings fruity sweetness and herbaceous notes. Crispy fried onions and toasted coconut flakes add textural contrast, while fresh cilantro and lime bring brightness to every bite. Served on a buttered and toasted brioche bun, this sandwich delivers a perfect balance of spicy, sweet, sour, and creamy in every component.

1 teaspoon fish sauce or soy sauce
1/4 cup frozen peas, thawed and mashed
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split

In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and 1 tablespoon lime juice until combined.

In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, curry powder, turmeric, cumin, ginger powder, garlic powder, cayenne, and salt. Mix thoroughly to distribute seasonings evenly.
Dip the chicken breast into the wet batter, coating thoroughly on all sides. Let excess drip off.
Transfer to the dry batter and coat completely, pressing gently so the coating adheres. For extra crispiness, dip back into the wet batter and then into the dry batter a second time.
Heat beef tallow or lard in a heavy-bottomed pot or deep skillet to 350°F. Use a thermometer to maintain consistent temperature.

Remove the fried chicken with a slotted spoon and place on a wire rack (not paper towels) to cool slightly and maintain crispiness.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add 1/2 minced yellow onion and cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and beginning to turn translucent.
Add 1 teaspoon minced ginger and 2 minced garlic cloves; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in 2 teaspoons curry powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder, and 1 teaspoon cumin powder; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add 1/2 cup coconut milk and 2 tablespoons chicken stock; stir well.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice, 1 teaspoon fish sauce or soy sauce, and 1 teaspoon brown sugar.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Keep warm over low heat.

In a large bowl, combine 1 cup shredded red cabbage, 1/4 cup shredded carrots, 1/4 cup diced cucumber, 2 tablespoons thinly sliced red onions, 1 tablespoon chopped fresh mint, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons mango chutney, 2 tablespoons plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon lime juice, and 1/4 teaspoon cumin powder.
Pour the mango-yogurt dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Refrigerate until ready to use.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook 4 strips of diced thick-cut bacon until crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove half the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add 1/2 diced yellow onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves and 1 teaspoon minced ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in 1 teaspoon curry powder and cook for 30 seconds.
Add 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar, 2 tablespoons coconut milk, and 1 teaspoon lime juice.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Season with salt to taste. Let cool slightly — it will thicken as it cools.
In a small bowl, combine 2 ounces softened cream cheese and 1 ounce fresh goat cheese; mix until smooth.
Mash 1/4 cup thawed frozen peas lightly with a fork and fold into the cream cheese.

In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast 2-3 tablespoons sweetened coconut flakes, stirring frequently, for 2-3 minutes until light golden and fragrant.
Remove to a plate and set aside.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes per side until golden and fragrant.
Spread the Samosa Coconut Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Add a layer of Coconut Curry Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Place the fried chicken on the jam.
Spoon 2-3 tablespoons of warm Coconut Curry Sauce over the chicken.
Pile the Mango Chutney Slaw on top of the sauce.
Scatter crispy fried onions and toasted coconut flakes over the slaw.
Sprinkle fresh cilantro over the toppings.
Cap with the toasted top bun.
Serve immediately with a lime wedge on the side.

d: Inspired by the viral chopped Italian sandwich, this fried chicken version takes the classic deli sub to the next level. The crispy chicken is dunked in a spicy Italian oil-vinegar sauce loaded with pepperoncini and Italian seasoning, then topped with a chopped Italian salad of salami, provolone, lettuce, tomatoes, red onions, and banana peppers. A pepperoni cherry tomato jam on the bottom sub roll adds a sweet-savory Italian depth that ties the whole thing together.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
Marinara Basil Goat Feta Roasted Pepper Spread
dir: In a small skillet over medium heat, cook diced pepperoni for 2-3 minutes until it renders fat and begins to crisp.
Add finely diced onion and minced garlic, cooking for 2 minutes until softened.
Add quartered cherry tomatoes, chopped sun-dried tomatoes, brown sugar, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down and mixture becomes thick and jammy.
Season with salt. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, olive oil, and red wine vinegar until emulsified.
Stir in minced pepperoncini peppers, pepperoncini brine, Italian seasoning, minced garlic, and red pepper flakes.
Season with salt and black pepper. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine baby arugula, shredded red cabbage, halved cherry tomatoes, sliced red onions, and crumbled feta cheese.
Add sliced pepperoncini peppers, sliced cherry peppers, chopped salami, and crushed croutons.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, red wine vinegar, extra virgin olive oil, and Italian seasoning.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese and fresh goat cheese, mixing until smooth.
Fold in crumbled feta cheese, diced roasted red peppers, and mashed roasted garlic cloves.
Stir in marinara sauce, chopped fresh basil, red wine vinegar, and garlic powder.
Season with salt and black pepper. Set aside.
Pound the chicken cutlet to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, dried oregano, garlic powder, dried basil, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper.
Submerge chicken in wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Remove from wet batter and dredge thoroughly in dry batter, pressing gently to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Carefully place breaded chicken into hot oil and fry for 6-7 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove with slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack (not paper towels).
Butter both halves of the sub roll and toast on a griddle or skillet for 1-2 minutes until golden.
Spread Marinara Basil Goat Feta Roasted Pepper Spread on the bottom sub roll.
Spoon a generous layer of Pepperoni Cherry Tomato Jam over the spread.
Place the fried chicken on top of the jam.
Drizzle Italian Oil-Vinegar Pepperoncini Sauce over the chicken.
Pile Italian Arugula Slaw on top.
Sprinkle chopped salami and provolone cheese.
Top with crispy fried onions.
Place top bun and serve immediately while hot.

d: This rich Italian sandwich features a silky garlic Parmesan cream sauce draped over crispy fried chicken with Parmesan crisps and fried basil leaves. An Italian arugula slaw adds bright, fresh contrast while a pepperoni cherry tomato jam on the bottom sub roll brings sweet Italian depth. Shaved Parmigiano-Reggiano and baby arugula round out this sophisticated yet approachable sandwich.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
Lemon Butter Basil Goat Feta Roasted Pepper Spread
dir: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Place small mounds of grated Parmesan on a parchment-lined baking sheet, spacing them 2 inches apart.
Sprinkle each with dried Italian herbs.
Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy.
Remove and let cool on the baking sheet for 2 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.
Heat 1/2 cup beef tallow or lard to 300°F in a small skillet.
Carefully add fresh basil leaves and fry for 30 seconds until crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Season immediately with a pinch of salt.
In a small skillet over medium heat, cook diced pepperoni for 2-3 minutes until it renders fat and begins to crisp.
Add finely diced onion and minced garlic, cooking for 2 minutes until softened.
Add quartered cherry tomatoes, chopped sun-dried tomatoes, brown sugar, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down and mixture becomes thick and jammy.
Season with salt. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine baby arugula, shredded red cabbage, halved cherry tomatoes, sliced red onions, and crumbled feta cheese.
Add sliced pepperoncini peppers, sliced cherry peppers, chopped salami, and crushed croutons.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, red wine vinegar, extra virgin olive oil, and Italian seasoning.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese and fresh goat cheese, mixing until smooth.
Fold in crumbled feta cheese, diced roasted red peppers, and mashed roasted garlic cloves.

t: Chipotle Lime Chicken Sandwich - Smoky & Charred
d: A bold chipotle lime chicken sandwich that brings the heat of Mexican street food to a fried chicken foundation. Crispy fried chicken breast is smothered in a creamy chipotle adobo sauce, then layered with a tangy chipotle lime coleslaw loaded with cilantro and red cabbage. A sweet and spicy pineapple jalapeño bacon jam brings tropical depth on the bottom bun alongside a roasted corn and jalapeño goat cheese spread. Finished with pickled red onions, jalapeños, cotija cheese, and creamy avocado.
i: 2 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
3 peppers plus 1.5 tablespoons sauce chipotle peppers in adobo
1/2 pepper chipotle pepper in adobo, minced
1/2 pepper chipotle pepper in adobo, minced
as needed 1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun
as needed 1 tbsp unsalted butter, softened
as needed Pineapple jalapeño bacon jam
as needed Roasted corn jalapeño goat cheese spread
as needed Cotija cheese, crumbled (3 tbsp)
as needed Ripe avocado, sliced (1/4 avocado)
dir: Pat chicken breast dry with paper towels.
Whisk together buttermilk, egg, and fresh lime juice in a shallow bowl.
In another shallow bowl, combine flour, potato starch, chicken bouillon powder, chili powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Dip chicken into wet batter, coat thoroughly, then dredge in dry batter, pressing gently to adhere. Let rest on a plate for 5 minutes.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a heavy-bottomed pot or deep skillet, using a thermometer for accuracy.
Carefully place battered chicken into hot oil and fry for 6-7 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Drain on paper towels.
Combine mayonnaise, chipotle peppers and adobo sauce, lime juice, lime zest, minced garlic, and cilantro in a blender.
Blend until smooth, about 30 seconds.
Season with salt to taste.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, minced chipotle pepper, adobo sauce, lime juice, lime zest, apple cider vinegar, sugar, salt, and black pepper.
In a medium bowl, toss shredded green and red cabbage, shredded carrots, chopped cilantro, and sliced jalapeño together.
Pour the dressing over the slaw and toss to coat.
Refrigerate until ready to use.
In a small skillet, cook diced bacon over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until it begins to crisp and render fat.
Add diced jalapeño and diced onion, cooking for 2 minutes until softened.
Add diced pineapple, minced chipotle pepper, ancho chile powder, and sugar.
Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until the pineapple breaks down and becomes thick and jammy.
Season with salt. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese and goat cheese. Mix until smooth.
Fold in roasted corn kernels, finely minced jalapeño, chili powder, garlic powder, and salt until well combined.
Butter and toast the bun lightly until golden, about 1-2 minutes per side.
Spread the roasted corn jalapeño goat cheese spread on the bottom bun.
Spoon pineapple jalapeño bacon jam on top.
Place the chipotle sauce-coated chicken on the jam.
Pile the chipotle lime coleslaw on the chicken.
Top with pickled red onions, pickled jalapeños, crumbled cotija cheese, and sliced avocado.
Cap with the toasted top bun.
Serve immediately while the chicken is hot.

d: This refined French-style sandwich celebrates the sharp, sophisticated flavors of green peppercorns in every layer. Crispy fried chicken gets a luxurious brandy and cream sauce with crushed green peppercorns, then piled with sautéed leeks and melted gruyère. A tangy slaw, creamy peppercorn goat cheese spread, and a smoky bacon jam create a symphony of refined, elegant flavors.

dir: Combine 1/2 cup buttermilk and 1 egg in a bowl and whisk until smooth. Set aside wet batter.
In another bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup potato starch, 1 tsp chicken bouillon powder, 1/4 tsp white pepper, and 1/2 tsp salt. Set aside dry batter.
Pat 6-8 oz chicken breasts dry with paper towels.
Dip chicken into wet batter, coating completely, then dredge in dry batter, shaking off excess.
Heat 2 cups beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven using a thermometer.
Carefully place breaded chicken into hot fat and fry for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
Heat 2 tbsp unsalted butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add 2 minced shallots and cook 2 minutes until softened.
Add 2 tbsp drained green peppercorns and lightly crush with back of a spoon.
Pour in 2 tbsp brandy and simmer 1 minute to reduce.
Add 3/4 cup heavy cream and 2 tbsp beef broth, bring to gentle simmer.
Cook 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat and whisk in 1/2 tsp Dijon mustard.
Season with 1/4 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp white pepper.
Keep warm and reserve 2 tbsp for slaw dressing.
Clean 1 leek and slice the white and light green parts into 1/4-inch rounds.
Heat 1 tbsp unsalted butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Add leek slices and 2 fresh thyme sprigs.
Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and lightly caramelized.
Season with 1/8 tsp salt and a pinch of white pepper.
Discard thyme sprigs and set aside.
Whisk together 2 tbsp peppercorn cream sauce, 1 tbsp mayonnaise, 1/2 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, and a pinch of salt for the dressing.

In a large bowl, combine 1/2 cup shredded red cabbage, 2 tbsp thinly sliced raw leek, 1 tbsp shredded gruyère, 1 tsp fresh tarragon (chopped), 1 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped), 2 tbsp pickled red onions, and 1/2 tsp crushed green peppercorns.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Cook 4 slices diced thick-cut bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crispy, about 6-7 minutes.
Drain most fat, leaving about 1 tbsp in the pan.
Add 1 minced shallot and cook 2 minutes.
Add 1 tbsp crushed green peppercorns and 1/2 tsp fresh thyme leaves, cook 1 minute.
Deglaze with 1 tbsp brandy, simmer 30 seconds.
Add 1/2 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, and 2 tbsp water.
Simmer on low for 15-18 minutes until thick and jammy.
Let cool slightly and roughly chop to a spreadable consistency.
Mix 1 tbsp softened cream cheese and 1 tbsp softened goat cheese together until smooth.
Stir in 1/2 tsp crushed green peppercorns, 1/4 tsp Dijon mustard, 1/4 tsp fresh thyme leaves, and a pinch of salt.
Mix until evenly combined and ready to spread.
Butter the potato bun and toast in a skillet until golden on both sides.
Spread Peppercorn Goat Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Add a layer of Brandy Peppercorn Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Place the fried chicken on the bottom bun.
Layer sautéed leeks over the chicken.
Top with 2 slices of gruyère cheese, allowing it to melt from the heat of the chicken.
Spoon Green Peppercorn Cream Sauce generously over the cheese and chicken.
Top with Peppercorn Leek Slaw and fresh tarragon.

Let cool slightly and roughly chop to a spreadable consistency.
Mix 1 tbsp softened cream cheese and 1 tbsp softened goat cheese together until smooth.
Stir in 1 tsp fresh dill (finely minced), 1/4 tsp lemon zest, 1/2 tsp fresh lemon juice, 1 mashed roasted garlic clove, and a pinch of salt.

Layer sautéed spinach over the chicken.
Top with fresh mozzarella, allowing it to melt from the heat.
Spoon Lemon Butter Cream Sauce generously over the cheese and spinach.
Top with Lemon Herb Romaine Slaw and fresh dill.
Place top bun and serve immediately.

Mix 1 tbsp softened cream cheese and 1 tbsp softened goat cheese together until smooth.

Continue cooking, swirling occasionally, until the butter turns deep golden brown and smells nutty, about 5-7 minutes.
Add 2 chopped fresh medium peaches and 1 tbsp brown sugar.
Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in 2 tbsp bourbon whiskey and simmer 2 minutes to reduce.
Add 1/2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/8 tsp ground cinnamon, and 1/2 tsp fresh thyme leaves.
Simmer 1 more minute.
Season with 1/4 tsp salt and a pinch of black pepper.
Keep warm. Sauce should be thick and coat the back of a spoon.
In a small skillet, melt 1 tsp butter over medium heat.
Add 1/4 cup pecan halves, 1 tbsp brown sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Toss constantly for 3-4 minutes until the pecans are coated and sugar is caramelized.
Transfer to a parchment-lined plate to cool.
Pecans will crisp as they cool.
Thinly slice 1 medium yellow onion.
In a small bowl, combine 2 tbsp flour, 1 tbsp cornstarch, 1/4 tsp salt, and a pinch of cayenne pepper.
Toss onion slices with flour mixture until evenly coated.
Heat 1 cup beef tallow or lard to 325°F in a shallow pan.
Working in batches, carefully place coated onion straws into hot fat.
Fry 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy, stirring occasionally.
Transfer to paper towel-lined plate to drain.
For the dressing, mix together 1 tbsp cooled brown butter, 1 tsp apple cider vinegar, 1/2 tsp honey, 1/4 tsp Dijon mustard, and a pinch of salt.
In a bowl, combine 1/2 cup fresh arugula, 1/4 thinly sliced fresh peach, 1 tbsp chopped candied pecans, 1 tbsp shaved sharp white cheddar, and 3-4 fresh basil leaves (chiffonade).
Pour dressing over and toss gently to coat.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Cook 4 slices diced thick-cut bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crispy, about 6-7 minutes.
Drain most fat, leaving about 1 tbsp.
Add 1 minced shallot, cook 2 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup finely diced fresh peaches and cook 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add 1 tbsp bourbon whiskey, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, a pinch of ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp fresh thyme leaves, and 2 tbsp water.
Simmer on low for 15-18 minutes until thick and jammy.
Let cool and roughly chop to spreadable consistency.
Mix 1 tbsp softened cream cheese, 1 tbsp softened goat cheese, and 1 tbsp softened Brie (rind removed) until smooth.
Stir in 1 tsp cooled brown butter, 1/2 tsp bourbon whiskey, a pinch of ground cinnamon, and a pinch of salt.
Mix until evenly combined.
Butter the potato bun and toast in a skillet until golden on both sides.
Spread Bourbon Brown Butter Brie Goat Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Spread 1.5 tbsp Peach Bourbon Brown Butter Sauce on top.
Place the fried chicken on the bottom bun.
Layer 2 slices of sharp white cheddar cheese over the chicken.
Top with an additional 1.5 tbsp Peach Bourbon Brown Butter Sauce.
Pile fried onion straws generously on top for crunch.
Spread any remaining sauce on the top bun.
Place top bun and serve immediately while onion straws are crispy.
