d: Texas Roadhouse meets a charcuterie board — that famous sweet cinnamon honey butter gets drizzled over crispy fried chicken with warm baked Brie melting on top, caramelized apples, and apple jelly. An apple walnut slaw adds crunch and freshness, a caramelized apple bacon jam and a cinnamon honey butter Brie cream cheese spread load up the bottom bun. Onion rings pile on the comfort. Sweet, buttery, warm, and indulgent.
i: 1 onion yellow onion (sliced into thick rings)
as needed beef tallow or lard (for frying)
Caramelized Apple Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Cinnamon Honey Butter Brie Cream Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
Cinnamon Honey Brown Butter Sauce (drizzled over chicken)
dir: Combine 1/2 cup buttermilk and 1 egg in a bowl and whisk until smooth. Set aside wet batter.
In another bowl, whisk together all dry batter ingredients. Set aside dry batter.
Pat 6-8 oz chicken breasts dry with paper towels.
Dip chicken into wet batter, coating completely, then dredge in dry batter, shaking off excess.
Heat 2 cups beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven.
Carefully place breaded chicken into hot fat and fry for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
Toast the bottom and top of the bun until lightly golden.
Spread condiments and spreads on the bottom bun.
Layer toppings as indicated.
Place the fried chicken on the prepared bun.
Add all remaining toppings.
Close with top bun and serve immediately while the chicken is hot.

d: Portuguese-African fire on a bun — peri peri sauce made with bird's eye chilies, roasted red pepper, garlic, lemon, and red wine vinegar gets drizzled over crispy chicken that's already got smoked paprika and cayenne in the batter. A charred lemon slaw keeps it fresh, a roasted red pepper bacon jam and a peri peri garlic goat cheese spread load up the bottom bun. Smoky, spicy, tangy, and addictive — this is the Nando's sandwich you wish existed.
i: 2-3 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
Roasted Red Pepper Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Peri Peri Garlic Goat Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar.
In another shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
Toast the bottom and top of the bun until lightly golden.
Spread condiments and spreads on the bottom bun.
Layer toppings as indicated.
Place the fried chicken on the prepared bun.
Add all remaining toppings.
Close with top bun and serve immediately while the chicken is hot.

d: Classic French comfort on a bun — chicken fricassee is a creamy white wine sauce with mushrooms, pearl onions, tarragon, and thyme, and it gets poured right over crispy fried chicken. Sautéed mushrooms and melted Gruyère pile on the richness, a tarragon herb slaw adds freshness, and a mushroom Dijon bacon jam with a Gruyère herb goat cheese spread hold the bottom bun together. Elegant, creamy, and deeply savory.
i: 2-3 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
Mushroom Dijon Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Herb Mashed Potatoes (schmear on bottom bun)
Gruyère Herb Goat Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and 2 tablespoons white wine.
In another shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and dried thyme.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
Toast the bottom and top of the bun until lightly golden.
Spread condiments and spreads on the bottom bun.
Layer toppings as indicated.
Place the fried chicken on the prepared bun.
Add all remaining toppings.
Close with top bun and serve immediately while the chicken is hot.

d: The most iconic French dish of all time as a chicken sandwich — a rich, velvety red wine reduction made with Burgundy, bacon lardons, pearl onions, mushrooms, garlic, and thyme gets smothered over crispy fried chicken. Herb mashed potatoes schmeared on the bun, sautéed mushrooms on top, Gruyère melted over everything. A red wine herb slaw adds freshness, and a mushroom red wine bacon jam with a Gruyère thyme goat cheese spread hold the bottom bun. This is fine French dining between two buns.
i: 2-3 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
1 cup Burgundy wine or Pinot Noir
Mushroom Red Wine Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Gruyère Thyme Goat Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
Herb Mashed Potatoes (schmear on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and 2 tablespoons red wine.
In another shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and dried thyme.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
Toast the bottom and top of the bun until lightly golden.
Spread condiments and spreads on the bottom bun.
Layer toppings as indicated.
Place the fried chicken on the prepared bun.
Add all remaining toppings.
Close with top bun and serve immediately while the chicken is hot.

d: A dazzling wet lemon pepper glazed fried chicken sandwich that combines bright citrus flavors with creamy, tangy cheese. Crispy fried chicken breast is tossed in a warm lemon pepper butter sauce and layered with a fresh feta and arugula slaw, pickled red onions, fried tomato slices, and candied pork belly. The roasted garlic and feta cream cheese spread adds a rich, savory foundation that perfectly balances the zesty citrus notes throughout this sophisticated yet indulgent creation.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
4 oz pork belly, sliced into 1/4-inch strips
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
Roasted Garlic Feta Cream Cheese Spread
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg until combined.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, lemon pepper seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly to distribute seasonings.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a small saucepan over medium-low heat, melt the butter.
Add fresh lemon juice, lemon pepper seasoning, minced garlic, and salt.
Whisk until combined and warmed through, about 2 minutes.
Keep warm on low heat until ready to use.
In a large bowl, combine shredded red cabbage, carrots, and fresh arugula.
Add crumbled feta cheese and pickled red onions.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, lemon juice, lemon zest, vinegar, sugar, and celery seed.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook diced bacon until crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove half the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in lemon juice, lemon zest, brown sugar, black pepper, and apple cider vinegar.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Season with salt. Let cool slightly—it will thicken as it cools.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese, crumbled feta, and mashed roasted garlic.
Mix until smooth and well blended.
Stir in fresh dill. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
Pat pork belly strips dry with paper towels and season with salt and black pepper.
Heat a cast iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Place pork belly strips in the hot skillet and cook for 3-4 minutes per side until the edges are crispy.
Reduce heat to medium and continue cooking until internal portions are tender, about 2-3 more minutes.
Remove to a wire rack. While still warm, sprinkle with sugar and let cool slightly to caramelize.
Pat tomato slice dry with paper towels.
In a shallow bowl, combine flour, salt, black pepper, and garlic powder.
Dip tomato slice into buttermilk, then coat thoroughly with the flour mixture.
Heat 1/4 inch of beef tallow or lard in a skillet to 325°F.
Fry tomato for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and slightly softened.
Drain on a paper towel briefly before serving.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread Roasted Garlic Feta Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Spoon a generous layer of Lemon Pepper Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Toss the warm fried chicken in the Lemon Pepper Wet Sauce until evenly coated.
Place the sauce-coated chicken on top of the jam.
Pile on the Lemon Pepper Slaw.
Add candied pork belly strips and fried tomato slice.
Top with the top bun and serve immediately.

t: Fried Pickle & Tomato BLT Chicken Sandwich
d: A fresh, flavorful take on the classic BLT that brings together crispy fried chicken, tomatoes, and bacon without the traditional pickle element in the spread. Crispy fried chicken breast is topped with fresh tomato Italian seasoning mayo and layered with a crispy BLT slaw, bacon jam made with tomato paste, and a roasted garlic goat cheese spread. The real stars are the fried tomatoes and fried bacon strips that add textural contrast and bold flavor throughout.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg until combined.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, dill, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise and finely diced fresh tomato.
Add Italian seasoning and garlic powder.
Whisk until smooth and well combined.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Set aside to allow flavors to meld.
In a large bowl, combine shredded red cabbage, carrots, and red onions.
Add crispy bacon crumbles to the vegetables.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, sugar, and celery seed.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook diced bacon until crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove half the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in tomato paste, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, and smoked paprika.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Season with salt. Let cool slightly—it will thicken as it cools.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese, fresh goat cheese, and mashed roasted garlic.
Mix until smooth and well blended.
Stir in garlic powder. Season with salt and black pepper.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
Pat tomato slices dry with paper towels.
In a shallow bowl, combine flour, salt, black pepper, and garlic powder.
Dip each tomato slice into buttermilk, then coat thoroughly with the flour mixture.
Heat 1/4 inch of beef tallow or lard in a skillet to 325°F.
Fry tomato slices for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and slightly softened.
Drain on a paper towel briefly before serving.
In a skillet over medium-high heat, cook thick-cut bacon strips until crispy, about 8-10 minutes.
Remove to a paper towel to drain and crisp.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread Roasted Garlic Goat Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Spoon a generous layer of BLT Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Place the fried chicken on top of the jam.
Spread Fresh Tomato Italian Mayo Sauce generously over the chicken.
Pile on the BLT Slaw.
Add fried tomato slices and crispy fried bacon strips.
Top with the top bun and serve immediately.

d: An elegant New Orleans-inspired sandwich that brings together crispy fried chicken with the coastal sophistication of remoulade sauce and fried calamari. The creamy goat cheese spread is enriched with marinara sauce, creating a rich Italian-Cajun fusion. Crispy fried calamari rings and shallots sit atop the chicken, which is coated in a traditional Cajun remoulade with capers, cornichons, and spicy mustard. This is a bold, complex sandwich for adventurous palates.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
1 tbsp seafood stock or clam juice
5 oz fresh or frozen calamari, cleaned and sliced into rings
as needed (to reach 325°F) beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and seafood stock until combined.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, Old Bay, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, Creole mustard, and fresh lemon juice.
Fold in finely chopped capers and cornichons.
Add minced garlic, Cajun seasoning, and hot sauce.
Stir in fresh minced parsley.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Refrigerate until ready to use.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese and fresh goat cheese.
Stir in marinara sauce, diced roasted red peppers, and garlic powder.
Add hot sauce to taste.
Mix until smooth and well blended.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
In a large bowl, combine shredded red cabbage, carrots, red onions, and fresh parsley.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, lemon juice, vinegar, sugar, celery seed, Cajun seasoning, and hot sauce.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook diced bacon until crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove half the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in Cajun seasoning, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, and hot sauce.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Season with salt. Let cool slightly—it will thicken as it cools.
Pat calamari rings dry with paper towels.
In a shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and Old Bay seasoning.
Dip calamari rings into buttermilk, then coat thoroughly with the flour mixture.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 325°F in a deep skillet or pot.
Fry calamari rings for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper towel.
Pat shallot slices dry with paper towels.
In a shallow bowl, combine flour, salt, and black pepper.
Dip shallot slices into the flour mixture, coating thoroughly.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 325°F in a deep skillet.
Fry shallot slices for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper towel.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread Marinara Cream Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Spoon a generous layer of Cajun Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Place the fried chicken on top of the jam.
Spread Cajun Remoulade Sauce generously over the chicken.
Pile on the Cajun Calamari Slaw.
Top with fried calamari rings and crispy fried shallots.
Serve with a fresh lemon wedge on the side.
Top with the top bun and serve immediately.

d: A bold, savory breakfast-inspired sandwich that transforms a breakfast bagel concept into a loaded chicken creation. Crispy fried chicken topped with a creamy everything bagel sauce made from mayo, sour cream, and cream cheese blended with everything bagel seasoning sits atop a bed of lox-style pickled red onions, ham, crispy bacon, cheddar cheese, and a fried egg. The everything bagel slaw provides a crunchy base, while fried tomato and fresh dill add brightness to this indulgent, over-the-top sandwich.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
1 everything bagel or seeded bun, split
Scallion Cream Cheese Goat Cheese Spread
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and softened cream cheese until well combined and smooth.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, everything bagel seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, sour cream, and softened cream cheese.
Whisk until smooth and creamy.
Add everything bagel seasoning and garlic powder.
Mix until well combined and evenly speckled with the seasoning.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Set aside or refrigerate until ready to use.
In a large bowl, combine shredded red cabbage, carrots, and red onions.
Sprinkle everything bagel seasoning and fresh dill over the vegetables.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, sugar, and celery seed.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook diced bacon until crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove half the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in everything bagel seasoning, brown sugar, and apple cider vinegar.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Season with salt and black pepper. Let cool slightly—it will thicken as it cools.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese, fresh goat cheese, and sour cream.
Mix until smooth and creamy.
Fold in fresh scallions, dill, and lemon zest.
Add everything bagel seasoning and mix until evenly distributed.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
In a small saucepan, combine rice vinegar, water, sugar, salt, coriander seeds, and dill seeds.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Place thinly sliced red onions in a glass jar or bowl.
Pour the hot brine over the onions and let cool to room temperature.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (or up to 1 week) before using.
Pat tomato slice dry with paper towels.
In a shallow bowl, combine flour, salt, black pepper, and garlic powder.
Dip tomato slice into buttermilk, then coat thoroughly with the flour mixture.
Heat 1/4 inch of beef tallow or lard in a skillet to 325°F.
Fry tomato for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and slightly softened.
Drain on a paper towel briefly before serving.
Heat 1 tbsp unsalted butter in a skillet over medium heat until foaming.
Crack the egg into the skillet and cook until the whites are set and the yolk is still runny, about 3-4 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Cook an additional 1-2 minutes if you prefer a more set yolk.
Slide the egg onto the sandwich.
Butter both halves of the everything bagel and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread Scallion Cream Cheese Goat Cheese Spread on the bottom bagel half.
Spoon a generous layer of Everything Bagel Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Place the fried chicken on top of the jam.
Spread Everything Bagel Sauce generously over the chicken.
Pile on the Everything Bagel Slaw.
Layer with ham slices, cheddar cheese, crispy bacon strips, lox-style pickled red onions, and fried tomato.
Top with a fried egg, fresh dill fronds, and optional brined capers.
Top with the top bagel half and serve immediately.

t: Red Wine Onion Gravy Chicken Sandwich
d: An elegant, sophisticated sandwich inspired by French beef stews and elevated comfort food. Crispy fried chicken is topped with a rich special steak sauce and layered with a deep, complex red wine beef stew (braised shredded beef, stewed vegetables, and herbs—no cabbage). Mashed potatoes are spread directly into the cheese spread for added creaminess, while a peppercorn gravy drizzles over everything. Salty crispy steak fries and melted sharp cheddar finish this restaurant-worthy creation that's as indulgent as it is refined.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
4 roasted and charred garlic cloves, mashed
3 tbsp roasted and charred red bell pepper, diced
3 tbsp roasted and charred red onion, diced
1/3 cup beef chuck roast, braised and shredded
2.5 tbsp beef drippings or unsalted butter
1 large potato russet potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch thick sticks
as needed (to reach 325°F) beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and red wine until combined.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, fresh thyme, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a heavy skillet, melt butter over medium heat.
Add minced shallots and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add mashed roasted garlic, diced charred red pepper, and diced charred red onion.
Cook for 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Reduce heat to low and add A1 sauce, mayonnaise, pepperoncini juice, lemon juice, and beef stock.
Whisk in fresh thyme, parsley, rosemary, and beef bouillon.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and season with salt, coarse black pepper, and optional Dijon mustard or horseradish.
Keep warm until ready to use.
In a large pot, heat 2 tbsp beef tallow or lard over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef chuck (cut into chunks) on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onions, carrots, and celery for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pot.
Add red wine, beef stock, tomato paste, fresh rosemary, thyme, and Worcestershire sauce.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Braise for 2.5-3 hours until beef is very tender and vegetables are fully cooked.
Remove beef from pot and shred using two forks.
Continue simmering vegetables and broth until vegetables are very soft and partially broken down, about 30 more minutes.
Return shredded beef to the pot and stir to combine.
Season with cracked black pepper and salt.
Use immediately or keep warm until ready to assemble sandwich.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook diced bacon until crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove half the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add diced onion and cook until softened and caramelized, about 5-6 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
In a small saucepan, simmer red wine over medium-high heat until reduced by half and syrupy, about 5 minutes.
Add the red wine reduction to the bacon and onion mixture along with fresh thyme, brown sugar, vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Season with salt and black pepper. Let cool slightly—it will thicken as it cools.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese and fresh goat cheese.
Add mashed potatoes to the mixture and blend until smooth and creamy.
Fold in mashed roasted garlic cloves.
Stir in fresh thyme and rosemary.
Season with cracked black pepper and salt.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
In a small saucepan over medium-low heat, melt beef drippings or butter.
Whisk in flour to create a roux and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Slowly whisk in beef stock, stirring to avoid lumps.
Add cracked peppercorns and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 3-4 minutes until thickened, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low and add heavy cream, whisking to combine.
Simmer for 2 more minutes.
Season with salt to taste.
Keep warm in a small pitcher or gravy boat for drizzling.
Cut russet potatoes into 1/2-inch thick sticks.
Place in a bowl of ice water and soak for at least 30 minutes (or up to 4 hours) to remove excess starch.
Pat potatoes dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 325°F in a deep pot or fryer.
Fry potatoes in batches for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper towel.
Season immediately with salt and coarse black pepper.
Keep warm until ready to serve.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread Red Wine Goat Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Spoon a generous layer of Red Wine Onion Bacon Jam on top of the spread.
Place the fried chicken on top of the jam.
Spread Special Steak Sauce generously over the chicken.
Spoon a generous portion of Red Wine Beef Stew on top of the chicken.
Drizzle Peppercorn Gravy over the stew.
Top with a slice of melted sharp cheddar cheese.
Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.
Top with the top bun.
Serve immediately with Crispy Fried Steak Fries on the side.
Optional: Drizzle additional gravy over the top of the finished sandwich.

d: A luxurious, restaurant-inspired sandwich that brings together classic steakhouse flavors with fried chicken. Crispy fried chicken topped with a generous portion of creamy, butter-rich creamed spinach sits atop layers of braised beef stew, mashed potatoes, and a peppery creamy horseradish sauce. NO slaw, NO bacon jam—instead, fried onion straws and melted provolone add textural contrast and richness. The spinach artichoke goat cheese spread provides a flavorful base, making this a sophisticated, indulgent creation for serious comfort food enthusiasts.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
1/3 cup beef chuck roast, braised and shredded
2/3 cup russet potatoes, boiled and mashed
2 tbsp chopped fresh or cooked spinach
1 large onion onions, cut into thin straws
as needed (to reach 325°F) beef tallow or lard for frying
1 yellow potato bun or brioche bun, split
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and heavy cream until smooth and combined.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, nutmeg, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine sour cream and mayonnaise until smooth.
Add extra hot prepared horseradish, stirring well to combine.
Fold in minced raw garlic and finely minced red onions.
Add fresh lemon juice and red wine vinegar.
Stir in melted butter until emulsified.
Season with coarse black pepper and salt to taste.
Stir in optional fresh dill if desired.
Refrigerate until ready to use. The flavors will meld and deepen as it sits.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, melt 4 tbsp butter.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add packed fresh spinach in batches, stirring until wilted. This may take 5-7 minutes as the spinach releases water.
Once all spinach is wilted, reduce heat to medium-low.
Cut cream cheese into small cubes and add to the spinach, stirring until melted and combined.
Add heavy cream slowly while stirring, incorporating it fully.
Fold in grated Parmesan cheese and stir until melted and smooth.
Season with a whisper of nutmeg, salt, and black pepper.
Keep warm on low heat until ready to serve. Stir occasionally.
In a large pot, heat 2 tbsp beef tallow or lard over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef chuck (cut into chunks) on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onions, carrots, and celery for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pot.
Add beef stock and bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2.5-3 hours until beef is very tender.
Remove beef from pot and shred using two forks.
Continue simmering vegetables in the broth until very soft, about 30 more minutes.
Return shredded beef to the pot and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper.
Use immediately or keep warm.
Peel and cube russet potatoes.
Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain thoroughly in a colander.
Return to the pot and mash with a potato ricer or masher until smooth.
Fold in butter and heavy cream while the potatoes are still warm.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Keep warm until ready to assemble.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese and fresh goat cheese.
Fold in chopped artichoke hearts and chopped spinach.
Add grated Parmesan cheese and mashed roasted garlic.
Stir in garlic powder.
Mix until smooth and well combined.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Spread on the bottom bun before assembling.
Pat onion straws dry with paper towels.
In a shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, salt, and black pepper.
Toss onion straws in the flour mixture, coating thoroughly.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 325°F in a deep skillet or pot.
Fry onion straws in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden and crispy, stirring occasionally.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper towel.
Season lightly with additional salt if desired.
Butter both halves of the bun and toast on a griddle or skillet until golden, about 2 minutes.
Spread Spinach Artichoke Goat Cheese Spread on the bottom bun.
Layer mashed potatoes on top of the spread.
Spoon braised beef stew on top of the potatoes.
Place the fried chicken on top of the stew.
Generously ladle creamed spinach over the chicken, allowing it to cascade down.
Drizzle Creamy Horseradish Sauce over the spinach.
Layer fried onion straws on top.
Place a slice (or two) of provolone cheese on top and let it begin to melt from the warm chicken.
Top with the top bun and serve immediately.

d: An audacious, carb-on-carb indulgent creation that places crispy fried chicken atop a split, loaded baked potato instead of a traditional bun. Beer cheese and bacon bits form the primary sauce, while white onions and fried onion strips add layers of savory crunch. The chicken rests directly on the warm, fluffy potato interior that's been dressed with sour cream and sharp cheddar cheese. There's NO hash brown patty, NO slaw—just a celebration of crispy, fried, and loaded comfort food at its most extreme.
i: 2 quarts (for heating) beef tallow or lard for frying
1 large onion white onions, cut into thin strips
as needed (to reach 325°F) beef tallow or lard for frying
Loaded Baked Potato (serves as the base, no traditional bun)
Sour Cream and Onion Potato Chip Crumbles (garnish)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and sour cream until well combined.
In another shallow bowl, combine all-purpose flour, potato starch, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and salt. Mix thoroughly.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F.
Scrub the russet potato under running water and pat dry.
Poke holes all over the potato with a fork.
Place directly on the oven rack and bake for 50-60 minutes until a fork pierces the flesh easily.
Remove from oven and let cool slightly for 2-3 minutes.
Cut the potato in half lengthwise.
Using a spoon, carefully scoop the interior, leaving about 1/4 inch of potato skin intact to maintain structure.
Mash the scooped interior slightly and return half to each potato half.
Top the potato halves with butter, sour cream, sharp cheddar cheese, bacon crumbles, diced white onions, and chives.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Keep warm until ready to assemble the sandwich.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese and fresh goat cheese.
Fold in mashed potato until the mixture is smooth and creamy.
Add shredded sharp cheddar cheese, bacon crumbles, and minced chives.
Stir in sour cream until well combined.
Add garlic powder and black pepper.
Mix until smooth and spreadable.
Season with salt to taste.
Use to line the interior of the loaded potato halves or spread underneath the chicken.
In a small saucepan over medium-low heat, warm the beer cheese sauce gently, stirring occasionally.
Add sour cream and whisk until smooth and creamy.
Fold in crispy bacon bits.
Add buttermilk slowly to reach desired consistency—the sauce should be pourable but still creamy.
Stir in minced chives, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper.
Season with salt to taste.
Keep warm over low heat, stirring occasionally, until ready to use.
In a skillet over medium-high heat, cook thick-cut bacon strips until crispy, about 8-10 minutes.
Remove to a paper towel to drain and crisp.
Pat white onion strips dry with paper towels.
In a shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, salt, and black pepper.
Toss onion strips in the flour mixture, coating thoroughly.
Heat beef tallow or lard to 325°F in a deep skillet or pot.
Fry onion strips in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden and crispy, stirring occasionally.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper towel.
Season lightly with additional salt if desired.
Place the loaded baked potato halves (or use one large half as the base) on a serving plate or baking sheet.
Spread or spoon Loaded Potato Goat Cheese Spread generously into/around the potato.
Gently rest the fried chicken piece directly on top of the potato.
Drizzle Beer Cheese Bacon Sauce generously over the chicken and potato.
Top the chicken with a slice (or two) of sharp cheddar cheese and allow it to melt slightly.
Add crispy fried bacon strips on top of or alongside the chicken.
Pile fried onion strips on top for textural contrast.
Scatter fresh diced white onions around the plate for sharp allium flavor.
Garnish with sour cream and onion potato chip crumbles for an extra indulgent crunch.
Finish with fresh chives.
Serve immediately with a fork and knife (this is a loaded creation, not a traditional sandwich to grab!).

d: Greek street food meets fried chicken — cool, creamy tzatziki loaded with cucumber, garlic, and dill gets drizzled over crispy chicken with salty feta crumbles and crunchy fried pita shards. A Mediterranean slaw with tomato, cucumber, and red onion keeps it fresh, a sun-dried tomato bacon jam and a roasted garlic feta goat cheese spread hold the bottom bun. Oregano and lemon juice in the batter give the chicken that Greek flavor from the crust out.
i: 2-3 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
Mediterranean Slaw (lots of feta, red wine vinegar)
Sun-Dried Tomato Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Roasted Garlic Feta Goat Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
to taste red bell pepper (dehydrated, optional)
as needed beef tallow or lard (for frying)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and 1 tablespoon lemon juice.
In another shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and dried oregano.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
Toast the bottom and top of the bun until lightly golden.
Spread condiments and spreads on the bottom bun.
Layer toppings as indicated.
Place the fried chicken on the prepared bun.
Add all remaining toppings.
Close with top bun and serve immediately while the chicken is hot.

d: Middle Eastern street food royalty on a bun — the batter is loaded with shawarma spices (cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, cinnamon) so the chicken crust tastes like it came off a rotating spit. Toum — that insanely garlicky Lebanese whipped sauce — gets drizzled over everything. A fresh fattoush-style slaw, pickled turnips, and a tahini bacon jam bring the full shawarma cart experience to a fried chicken sandwich.
i: 2-3 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
Shawarma Spiced Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Shawarma Spiced Goat Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
Roasted Red Pepper Hummus (spread on bottom bun)

In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk, egg, and 1 tablespoon lemon juice.

Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
Toast the bottom and top of the bun until lightly golden.
Spread condiments and spreads on the bottom bun.
Layer toppings as indicated.
Place the fried chicken on the prepared bun.
Add all remaining toppings.
Close with top bun and serve immediately while the chicken is hot.

d: NYC halal cart legendary status on a bun — that famous white sauce (mayo, yogurt, garlic, lemon) that people line up around the block for gets drizzled all over crispy fried chicken. A Middle Eastern slaw with cucumber, pickled red onions, and sumac adds crunch and freshness, a lemon olive cream cheese spread and a garlic herb bacon jam load up the bottom bun. Hot sauce drizzle on top because that's how the cart guys do it. Late night Manhattan street food perfected.
i: 2 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
to taste salt and black pepper
Garlic Herb Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Lemon Olive Cream Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
Roasted Red Pepper Hummus (spread on bottom bun)
Halal White Sauce (drizzled generously over chicken)
dir: Combine 1/2 cup buttermilk and 1 egg in a bowl and whisk until smooth. Set aside wet batter.
In another bowl, whisk together all dry batter ingredients. Set aside dry batter.
Pat 6-8 oz chicken breasts dry with paper towels.
Dip chicken into wet batter, coating completely, then dredge in dry batter, shaking off excess.
Heat 2 cups beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven.
Carefully place breaded chicken into hot fat and fry for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
Toast the bottom and top of the bun until lightly golden.
Spread condiments and spreads on the bottom bun.
Layer toppings as indicated.
Place the fried chicken on the prepared bun.
Add all remaining toppings.
Close with top bun and serve immediately while the chicken is hot.

d: Yemeni fire meets fried chicken — zhug is a bright, spicy green chili sauce loaded with fresh cilantro, parsley, serrano peppers, and garlic that gets drizzled over crispy chicken. A fresh herb and feta slaw adds crunch, a spiced bacon jam and a zhug-spiked goat cheese spread load up the bottom bun. Pita chips for crunch and sumac-dusted red onions on top. Herby, spicy, and addictive.
i: 2-3 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
Spiced Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Zhug Feta Goat Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cumin, coriander, and cinnamon.

d: Cool and refreshing — a creamy mint yogurt sauce with garlic, lemon, and cumin drizzled over crispy fried chicken. Fresh cucumber, sumac-dusted tomatoes, pickled red onions, and za'atar bring the Mediterranean vibes. A cucumber mint feta slaw keeps it bright, a za'atar spiced bacon jam and a mint feta goat cheese spread load up the bottom bun. Pita chips for crunch. Light, herby, and perfect for when you want something fresh.
i: 2-3 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
1 small Roma tomato (diced, dusted with sumac)
Za'atar Spiced Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Mint Feta Goat Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cumin, and za'atar.

d: Greek mezze plate on a bun — tangy whipped feta with lemon, garlic, and red pepper flakes gets schmeared on the bottom bun under crispy fried chicken. Roasted red peppers, Kalamata olive tapenade, and fresh cucumber pile on top. A Greek slaw with feta and olives adds crunch, a sun-dried tomato olive bacon jam and the whipped feta spread load up the bottom bun. Pita chips for crunch. It's like ordering everything at a Greek restaurant and putting it on fried chicken.
i: 2-3 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
Sun-Dried Tomato Olive Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Sun-Dried Tomato Goat Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
Roasted Red Pepper Hummus (spread on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.

In another shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and dried oregano.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).

d: Moroccan street food vibes — chermoula is a bold, herby North African paste packed with cilantro, parsley, garlic, cumin, paprika, preserved lemon, and olive oil that gets drizzled over crispy fried chicken. Pickled carrots add tang, toasted pine nuts bring crunch, and crumbled goat cheese adds creaminess. A Moroccan spiced slaw keeps it fresh, a preserved lemon bacon jam and a chermoula goat cheese spread hold the bottom bun. Bright, herby, and exotic.
i: 2-3 cups beef tallow or lard for frying
Moroccan Spiced Slaw (with feta and pine nuts)
Preserved Lemon Bacon Jam (spread on bottom bun)
Chermoula Goat Cheese Spread (spread on bottom bun)
dir: Pound the chicken breast to an even 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In another shallow bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, sweet paprika, cumin, and coriander.
Submerge the chicken in the wet batter for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).
Heat beef tallow or lard to 350°F in a deep pot or cast iron skillet.
Remove chicken from wet batter, letting excess drip off. Dredge thoroughly in the dry batter, pressing to adhere. For extra crunch, dip back in wet batter and dredge again.
Fry for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest on a wire rack for 2 minutes.

Layer toppings as indicated.
Place the fried chicken on the prepared bun.

Close with top bun and serve immediately while the chicken is hot.

d: Beef Pot Pie Crockpot Dip is a cozy, hearty blend of chuck steak, ground beef, and garden-fresh vegetables like mushrooms, peas, and carrots, all simmered to perfection. The rich flavor of garlic combined with the savory depth of the meats creates a comforting dip that’s perfect for gatherings. Serve it with crusty bread and watch it disappear as guests savor every creamy, meaty bite!
i: 1 lb chuck steak, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of mushroom soup
dir: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the chuck steak cubes and ground beef until no longer pink, about 8 minutes. Drain excess fat and transfer meat to a 6-quart crockpot.
Add the mushrooms, cabbage, carrots, peas, celery, red pepper, red onion, and garlic to the crockpot. Stir in the hash browns and stuffing mix.

In a medium bowl, whisk together the beef stock, horseradish, mustard, beef gravy mix, stroganoff seasoning, au jus seasoning, cream of mushroom soup, and Worcestershire sauce. Pour over the meat and vegetables in the crockpot.
Add the butter, black pepper, thyme, rosemary, and bouillon cubes. Stir everything together until well combined.
Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours or high for 3-4 hours, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender and mixture is thick and bubbly.
About 15 minutes before serving, stir in the Parmesan cheese and fresh parsley. Adjust seasoning with additional pepper if needed.
Serve hot with crackers, bread, or tortilla chips. Garnish with lemon slices if desired for a bright finishing touch.

t: BBQ Pork Pot Pie Crockpot Dip
d: BBQ Pork Pot Pie Crockpot Dip is a comforting blend of Jimmy Dean's sausage and tender shredded pork shoulder, mixed with colorful veggies like corn, jalapeños, and green beans. Infused with aromatic herbs like thyme and rosemary, this dip bursts with flavor, making it a crowd-pleaser at any party. Pair it with tortilla chips, and enjoy the smoky, savory goodness that’s sure to leave everyone craving more!
i: 1 cup Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ Sauce or Devil Spit
2 cans (10.5 oz each) cream of chicken soup
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of mushroom soup (optional)
dir: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the Jimmy Dean's sausage, breaking it into crumbles. Drain excess fat and transfer to a 6-quart crockpot.
Add shredded pork shoulder, all vegetables (corn, peas, green beans, jalapeños, carrots, celery, red onion), hash browns, garlic, thyme, rosemary, and parsley to the crockpot.
Stir in BBQ sauce, cream of chicken soup (and cream of mushroom if using), whole grain mustard, cream cheese (cut into chunks), heavy cream, and 1 cup of the cheddar cheese until well combined.
Cover and cook on low for 4-5 hours or high for 2-3 hours, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender and everything is heated through.
About 30 minutes before serving, stir in remaining cheddar and pepper jack cheese until melted and smooth.
Top with stuffing mix, cover, and cook for final 20-25 minutes until stuffing is slightly crispy on top.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste, garnish with extra parsley, and serve hot with tortilla chips, crackers, or bread.

d: Savor the warmth of Chicken Pot Pie Crockpot Dip, a sumptuous blend of shredded rotisserie chicken and crispy bacon, combined with a medley of vegetables such as hash browns and green beans. The garlic and jalapeños add a delightful kick, while the creamy base envelops you in comfort. Perfect for sharing, this dip is a delicious twist on a classic that will have everyone reaching for seconds!
i: 16 oz cream cheese, softened and cubed
2 (10.5 oz) cans cream of chicken soup
Puff pastry, biscuits, or croissants for serving
Optional: 1 lb pork belly or pork shoulder, diced and cooked
dir: In a large skillet, brown the Jimmy Dean's sausage over medium-high heat, breaking it into crumbles. Drain and transfer to a 6-quart crockpot.
Add the shredded rotisserie chicken, crumbled bacon, all vegetables (hash browns, green beans, corn, carrots, onion, peas, garlic, celery, jalapeños), and stuffing mix to the crockpot.

In a medium saucepan over low heat, combine the butter, cream cheese, cream of chicken soup, heavy cream, chicken bouillon, Worcestershire sauce, and hot sauce. Stir until smooth and melted, then pour over the ingredients in the crockpot.
Add the thyme, rosemary, parsley, and black pepper. Stir everything together to combine well.
Cover and cook on low for 4-5 hours or high for 2-3 hours, stirring occasionally.
About 30 minutes before serving, stir in the mozzarella, cheddar, and pepper jack cheeses until melted and incorporated.
Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or hot sauce to taste. Serve hot with warm puff pastry squares, biscuits, or croissants for dipping.

d: Dive into this luscious creamy roasted tomato garlic sauce, where vibrant cherry tomatoes and sweet, caramelized garlic take center stage. With a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a pat of butter, this sauce bursts with flavor from the oven-roasted goodness. Perfect for pasta, it's a comforting delight that elevates any dish with its rich, tangy depth.
dir: Preheat oven to 400°F. Spread cherry tomatoes, garlic cloves, and red onion quarters on a large baking sheet.
Drizzle with olive oil and dot with butter, then season with salt and pepper. Roast for 30-35 minutes until tomatoes are bursting and garlic is golden and soft.
Transfer roasted vegetables to a blender or food processor. Add basil, Italian seasoning, black pepper, sour cream, Greek yogurt, whipped feta, parmesan, and cottage cheese if using.
Blend until smooth and creamy, scraping down sides as needed. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
If sauce is too thick, thin with a splash of pasta water or milk. Serve warm over pasta, or let cool and use as a dip.

t: Creamy Lemon Roasted Garlic Herb Sauce
d: This creamy lemon roasted garlic herb sauce is a delightful blend of soft, caramelized garlic infused with zesty lemon and fresh herbs. The melted butter creates a velvety base that captures the buttery sweetness of the roasted garlic. Ideal for drizzling over grilled chicken or veggies, this sauce will awaken your taste buds and add a fresh, herbaceous twist to your meals.
dir: Preheat oven to 400°F. Cut the top off the garlic head, drizzle with olive oil, wrap in foil, and roast for 35-40 minutes until soft and golden. Let cool, then squeeze out the cloves.
In a medium saucepan over low heat, melt the butter. Add the roasted garlic cloves and mash them into the butter with a fork.
Add sour cream, Greek yogurt, feta, cottage cheese, and chicken bouillon to the pan. Stir constantly over low heat until smooth and warmed through, about 3-4 minutes. Don't let it boil.
Remove from heat and stir in lemon juice and all the fresh herbs. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve warm or let cool and refrigerate. The sauce will thicken as it cools and keeps well for up to 5 days.

d: Experience the mouthwatering combination of fluffy potatoes, tangy goat cheese, and vibrant pesto in these decadent muffins. Coated in a buttery flour mixture, these savory delights are baked to perfection, creating a heavenly texture that's both crispy on the outside and soft within. These muffins are an irresistible side dish or snack that will leave you craving more!
dir: Bake potatoes at 400°F until tender, about 45 minutes. Let cool slightly, then roll each potato in melted butter. In a small bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, baking powder, and 1 teaspoon salt. Coat buttered potatoes in this mixture.

Place coated potatoes in a greased muffin tin. Use the bottom of a seasoning jar or small glass to press down on each potato, creating a pocket in the center. Bake at 425°F for 20-25 minutes until crispy and golden.
While potatoes bake, mix together pesto, roasted garlic, goat cheese, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, and feta in a bowl until well combined. Set aside.

In another bowl, combine cherry tomatoes, red onion, cucumber, corn, cherry peppers, basil, olive oil, red wine vinegar, balsamic glaze, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt. Fold in crushed kettle chips just before serving.
Remove crispy potato cups from oven and fill each with the pesto-cheese mixture. Return to oven at 350°F for 7 minutes to warm the filling.
Remove potato cups from muffin tin and place on a serving platter. Top each generously with the tomato salad mixture, filling the potato pockets completely.

d: Savor the delightful crunch of Mediterranean potato crunchies, where creamy mashed potatoes meet tangy feta cheese and fresh herbs like parsley and dill. The vibrant mix of red onion and tomato adds a burst of flavor, while a crispy breadcrumb coating gives each bite a satisfying crunch. Perfect as an appetizer or snack, these crunchies are a celebration of Mediterranean flavors that will keep you coming back for more!
i: 1/2 cup red bell pepper, finely diced
dir: In a large bowl, combine the cooled mashed potatoes, feta, parsley, cilantro, dill, red onion, tomato, and red pepper. Mix well.
Add the flour, cornstarch, breadcrumbs, salt, and pepper to the potato mixture. Stir until everything is well combined and the mixture holds together.
Form the mixture into patties about 3 inches wide and 1/2 inch thick. Place on a plate or baking sheet.
Heat about 1/4 inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Working in batches, carefully place the patties in the hot oil and fry for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer the fried patties to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve hot with spicy tzatziki sauce for dipping.

d: Elevate your salads with this zesty Southwest salad dressing, bursting with flavor from creamy Greek yogurt, smoky chipotle peppers, and tangy lime juice. Each spoonful is a harmonious blend of spices, including chili powder and garlic powder, creating a deliciously bold kick that's perfect for drizzling over crisp greens. It's not just a dressing; it's a flavor explosion that will transform your salads into something truly unforgettable!
i: 1 cup Greek yogurt (or ½ cup mayo and ½ cup sour cream)
2-3 chipotle peppers in adobo, finely chopped
2 tablespoons adobo sauce from the can
1 tablespoon honey or finely grated apple (for sweetness)
dir: In a medium bowl, combine the Greek yogurt (or mayo and sour cream) with the chopped chipotle peppers, adobo sauce, and Cholula hot sauce.
Add the minced jalapeño, cilantro, garlic, lime juice, and apple cider vinegar. Stir well to combine.
Mix in all the dry spices: chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, black pepper, smoked paprika, and cumin.
Stir in the honey or grated apple to balance the heat with a touch of sweetness.
Taste and adjust seasoning — add more lime juice for tang, hot sauce for heat, or honey for sweetness.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving to let the flavors marry together. Keeps in the fridge for up to a week.

d: This vibrant Tasty Tuna Salad combines al dente penne pasta with flavorsome tuna and sharp cheddar cheese. Fresh cherry tomatoes, crunchy cucumber, and sweet peas elevate the dish, while a zesty dressing of mayonnaise and lemon juice brings it all together. Perfect for a light lunch or picnic, every bite is a refreshing explosion of taste!
i: 1 cup white corn (fresh, canned, or frozen)
dir: Cook penne pasta according to package directions, drain, and rinse with cold water to cool completely.
In a large bowl, combine cooled pasta, tuna, cheddar cheese, red onion, cherry tomatoes, bell pepper, cucumber, peas, and corn.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, lemon juice, olive oil, and Italian seasoning until smooth. Add wasabi if desired.
Pour dressing over pasta mixture and toss until everything is well coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to let flavors meld.
Just before serving, top with crumbled feta cheese and crushed kettle chips for crunch.

t: Fried Chicken Caesar Salad Pasta Bake
d: Imagine a delicious Fried Chicken Caesar Salad Pasta Bake that perfectly melds crispy fried chicken with creamy Caesar dressing and al dente penne pasta. Infused with garlic, red peppers, and savory bacon, this dish is the ultimate comfort food. It's baked to golden perfection, ensuring every forkful is a tasty, cheesy delight that will have everyone coming back for more!
i: 4 fried chicken thighs, chopped into bite-sized pieces
1 (14 oz) can artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
dir: Preheat oven to 375°F. Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente, drain and set aside.

In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add garlic and red peppers, cooking for 3-4 minutes until softened. Stir in red onions, tomatoes, pepperoni, artichoke hearts, and bacon, cooking for another 2-3 minutes.

In a large bowl, combine cooked pasta, vegetable mixture, chopped fried chicken, Caesar dressing, sour cream, lemon juice, black pepper, 1 cup mozzarella, and 1/2 cup Parmesan. Mix well until everything is evenly coated.
Transfer mixture to a greased 9x13 inch baking dish. Top with remaining mozzarella and Parmesan, then sprinkle crushed croutons over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly and croutons are golden brown.
Remove from oven and let cool for 5 minutes. Top with fresh chopped romaine lettuce and crumbled feta cheese before serving.

d: Mystic Macaroni Salad is a creamy and tangy side dish that brings macaroni to life with a luscious mixture of mayonnaise, sweet relish, and a hint of smoky paprika. The added crunch from fresh vegetables like red peppers and celery makes it irresistibly satisfying. This salad is perfect for barbecues or picnics, offering a nostalgic burst of flavor in every bite.
i: 8 slices bacon, cooked crispy and crumbled
1 cup corn (canned, drained, or frozen and thawed)
2 cups roasted chopped chicken thighs or smoked BBQ pulled pork
dir: Cook macaroni according to package directions, drain, and rinse with cold water. Let cool completely in the refrigerator while you prep the other ingredients.
In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, sugar, sweet relish, red pepper flakes, and smoked paprika until well combined.

Add the cooled macaroni, bacon, hard boiled eggs, cheddar cheese, red onion, celery, red pepper, carrots, tomatoes, corn, peas, and cucumber to the bowl. Toss everything together until evenly coated with the dressing.
Fold in the roasted chicken thighs or pulled pork. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to let the flavors meld together.
Just before serving, top the salad with crushed jalapeño kettle chips and drizzle with hot honey if desired.

d: Eggsalant Everything Egg Salad takes classic egg salad to new heights with hard-boiled eggs, crispy bacon, and a medley of vibrant veggies like jalapeños and cherry tomatoes. The creamy blend of mayo, mustard, and a kick of red pepper flakes creates an addictive flavor profile. It's a fantastic spread for sandwiches or can be enjoyed right out of the bowl!
i: 8 strips bacon, cooked crispy and crumbled
2 tablespoons yellow mustard or whole grain mustard
Optional: 1 cup corn kernels (fresh or canned, drained)
Optional: 2 medium potatoes, boiled and diced
dir: In a large mixing bowl, combine the chopped hard boiled eggs, crumbled bacon, pickles, celery, red onion, jalapeños, cucumber, red peppers, and cherry tomatoes.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together the mayo, mustard, sour cream, lemon juice, red pepper flakes, and black pepper until smooth.
Add the dill, parsley, and thyme to the egg mixture, then pour the dressing over everything and gently fold together until well combined.
Fold in the crumbled goat cheese, being careful not to mash it completely — you want some chunks.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more pepper, lemon juice, or salt if needed.
If using any optional ingredients (corn, croutons, potatoes, or avocado), gently fold them in just before serving.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to let the flavors meld together before serving.

t: Smoked and Candied BBQ Hotdog Burnt Ends
d: Dive into the smoky goodness of Smoked and Candied BBQ Hotdog Burnt Ends, where juicy hotdogs or kielbasa are transformed into savory bites. Coated in a sweet and tangy mixture of yellow mustard, honey, and a bold BBQ seasoning with a touch of jalapeño heat, these burnt ends are smoked to perfection. Perfect for game day or any gathering, they are a flavor-packed treat that will leave you craving more!
i: 2 lbs beef hotdogs or cheddar kielbasa sausages
1 cup devil spit BBQ sauce (or your favorite spicy BBQ sauce)
1/2 cup Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce
dir: Preheat smoker to 225°F. Cut hotdogs or kielbasa into 1½-inch chunks and place in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, mix together yellow mustard and honey. Pour over meat chunks and toss to coat evenly. This is your binder.
In another bowl, combine BBQ seasoning, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, and jalapeño seasoning. Sprinkle over the coated meat and toss until evenly covered.
Place seasoned meat chunks directly on smoker grates and smoke for 1½ to 2 hours, until edges start getting crispy and caramelized.
Transfer smoked chunks to a disposable aluminum pan. Drizzle with devil spit BBQ sauce and sprinkle with remaining 2 tablespoons brown sugar. Toss to coat.
Add butter pats and Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce to the pan, then cover tightly with foil. Increase heat to 400°F (or transfer to oven at 400°F).
Cook covered for 30 minutes, then remove foil and cook another 15-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce is thick and sticky and the burnt ends are glazed and caramelized.
Let cool for 5 minutes before serving with toothpicks. These are best served warm and sticky.

d: This Loaded Bratwurst Potato Salad is a hearty, smoky dish that combines tender potatoes with juicy bratwursts. Key ingredients like crispy bacon, tangy mustard, and fresh chives elevate each bite, making for an irresistible side. It's creamy yet robust, perfect for BBQs or family gatherings, delivering a burst of flavor that will have everyone coming back for seconds!
i: 4 lbs russet potatoes (or frozen hash browns)
2 lbs assorted bratwurst (beer, cheese, hot, and/or sweet & spicy)
1/4 cup whole grain mustard (or yellow mustard)
Salt and black pepper to taste
Hot beer cheese sauce for drizzling (optional)
dir: Cook bacon in a large skillet until crispy, then set aside. If using fresh potatoes, dice into 1-inch cubes and boil until fork-tender, about 15 minutes. If using hash browns, cook according to package directions until golden.

Fire up the grill and cook the bratwursts over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until nicely charred and cooked through, about 12-15 minutes. Let cool slightly, then slice into bite-sized pieces.
In a large bowl, combine mayo, mustard, sour cream, and Worcestershire sauce. Add garlic and mix well to create the dressing.
In a very large serving bowl, combine the cooked potatoes, sliced bratwurst, bacon, sauerkraut, all three onions, red peppers, jalapeños, pickles, tomatoes, green onions, and pepperoncini.
Pour the dressing over the potato mixture and toss gently to coat everything evenly. Fold in the pepper jack cheese.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve warm or at room temperature, drizzled with hot beer cheese if desired.

d: Dive into the decadence of Smoked 5 Cheese Spinach Artichoke Dip, a creamy and cheesy delight packed with smoked cream cheese, rich gouda, and tangy feta. The combination of sautéed onions, jalapeños, and garlic brings a burst of flavor that pairs perfectly with crunchy chips or toasted baguette slices. Ideal for gatherings or cozy nights in, this dip is sure to impress with its smoky richness and creamy texture!
i: 10 oz frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
14 oz artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
1/2 cup pepperoncini peppers or cherry peppers, chopped
dir: In a large skillet over medium heat, melt butter and sauté the onions, jalapeños, red peppers, and garlic (both minced and whole) until softened and fragrant, about 5-7 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the smoked cream cheese, gouda, parmesan, goat cheese, and feta. Stir in the heavy cream, smoked paprika, and black pepper until well mixed.
Add the squeezed spinach, chopped artichoke hearts, diced pepperoni, pepperoncini peppers, and the sautéed vegetable mixture to the cheese mixture. Fold everything together until evenly combined.
Transfer the dip to a cast iron skillet or oven-safe baking dish. Smoke at 225°F for 45-60 minutes, or bake at 350°F for 25-30 minutes until bubbly and golden on top.
Remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes. Drizzle with hot honey if desired, and serve warm with crackers, bread, or tortilla chips.

d: Sweet Sourkrout Meatballs are a deliciously unexpected comfort food, featuring tender meatballs and savory pork belly slow-cooked to perfection. The dish is made special with layers of tangy sauerkraut, sweet pineapple, and a unique sauce of chili sauce and grape jelly that creates an amazing sweet and savory balance. Perfect for a comforting dinner, this crockpot recipe is both easy and full of flavor!
i: 1 lb pork belly, cut into 1-inch cubes
1/2 cup Chick-fil-A Polynesian sauce or Catalina dressing (optional)
dir: Add meatballs and pork belly cubes to the bottom of a 6-quart crockpot.
Layer sauerkraut, sweet onion, orange pepper, pineapple chunks, carrots, and jalapeños over the meat.
In a medium bowl, whisk together chili sauce, grape jelly, orange juice, sugar, black pepper, and cayenne pepper until smooth. Pour evenly over everything in the crockpot.
Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours or high for 3-4 hours, stirring once halfway through if possible.
About 30 minutes before serving, stir in Polynesian sauce or Catalina dressing if using.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional sugar or black pepper if needed. Serve hot with toothpicks as an appetizer or over rice as a main dish.

t: Caramelized, Onion and Garlic Asian Fusion Spaghetti
d: Experience a flavor explosion with Caramelized Onion and Garlic Asian Fusion Spaghetti, where al dente angel hair pasta meets crispy pork belly and sweet, caramelized onions. The blend of butter and pork fat creates a rich base that beautifully complements the garlic, making each bite a savory delight. It's a fusion dish that’s both comforting and exciting, perfect for impressing dinner guests or satisfying a craving!
i: 1 lb pork belly, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
8 cloves garlic, 4 minced and 4 left whole
dir: Cook angel hair pasta according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
In a large skillet over medium heat, cook pork belly cubes until crispy and browned, about 8-10 minutes. Remove and set aside, leaving fat in pan.

Add butter and olive oil to the pork fat. Add sliced onions and cook low and slow until deeply caramelized, about 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add minced and whole garlic cloves during last 5 minutes.
Stir in chili crisp oil, soy sauce, paprika, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Reduce heat to low and add heavy cream, stirring to combine. Simmer for 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add Parmesan cheese and lemon juice, stirring until cheese melts and sauce is smooth.
Return pork belly to pan and toss cooked pasta in the sauce until well coated.
Serve immediately topped with fresh parsley and extra Parmesan if desired.

d: Crispy Chili Mayo Salad is a vibrant and zesty dish that tantalizes the taste buds with its combination of Greek yogurt, crispy chili oil, and Hoisin sauce. Shredded chicken or pork belly join forces with fresh veggies like cucumber and carrots, creating a refreshing crunch that contrasts beautifully with the creamy dressing. This salad is not just a side; it’s a flavor-packed experience that transforms any meal!
i: 2 cups shredded chicken or pork belly, cooked
1 cup corn kernels (fresh or canned, drained)
Optional: crunchy flattened potatoes for serving
dir: In a large bowl, whisk together Greek yogurt, mayo, crispy chili oil, sesame oil, and Hoisin sauce until smooth and well combined.
Add the shredded chicken or pork belly to the dressing and toss until evenly coated.
Add cucumber, carrots, green onions, red onions, and corn to the bowl. Toss everything together until vegetables are well mixed with the dressed meat.
Season with black pepper and adjust chili oil or Hoisin to taste if needed.
Gently fold in avocado chunks and sprinkle sesame seeds on top.
Serve immediately as is, or spoon over crunchy flattened potatoes for extra texture.

d: This Peppercorn Steak Sauce is a luxurious condiment perfect for elevating your steak. The rich combination of bourbon, heavy cream, and cracked black pepper creates a velvety sauce bursting with flavor. Its creamy texture and depth make every bite of steak irresistible, enticing anyone to whip this up for a gourmet meal at home.
dir: Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add shallots and garlic, cooking until softened and fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Add bourbon and let it simmer for 1 minute to cook off the alcohol. Stir in the steak gravy, heavy cream, and cracked black pepper.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Reduce heat to low and whisk in Parmesan cheese, mayo or sour cream, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar, and lemon juice until smooth.
Add thyme, rosemary, and parsley. Season with salt and adjust pepper to taste.
Simmer for another 2-3 minutes, then remove from heat. Serve warm over steak, potatoes, or as a dipping sauce for fries.

d: Bright and refreshing, this Tomato Pasta Salad is a delightful medley of rotini pasta, sautéed garlic, and zesty tomato paste. Tossed in a drizzle of olive oil and finished with a hint of butter, it's a perfect balance of flavors. With its vibrant colors and satisfying textures, this salad is a sure way to impress at any picnic or gathering.
i: 1 cup corn (fresh, canned, or thawed frozen)
dir: Cook rotini pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water, then set aside to cool completely.

Make the sauce: In a medium saucepan over medium heat, melt butter and sauté garlic and diced onions until softened, about 3 minutes. Stir in tomato paste, olive oil, Italian dressing, lemon juice, sugar, and Italian seasoning. Simmer for 5 minutes, then remove from heat and whisk in mayonnaise. Let cool to room temperature.
In a large bowl, combine cooled pasta, pepperoni, chicken, cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, bell pepper, corn, and parsley.
Pour the cooled sauce over the pasta mixture and toss until everything is well coated. Fold in feta cheese and pepperoncini if using.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving to let flavors meld. Toss again before serving and adjust seasoning if needed.

d: Start your day right with this Complete Breakfast Crockpot that's a hearty mix of breakfast sausage, crisp bacon, and sautéed vegetables like bell peppers and jalapeños. The slow-cooked blend of these savory ingredients creates a comforting and filling dish that's bursting with flavor. Perfect for busy mornings, this breakfast will have everyone rushing to the table for a delicious start.
i: 1 lb Jimmy Dean breakfast sausage (hot or maple style)
dir: In a large skillet, sauté the onion, garlic, bell pepper, jalapeños, and mushrooms (if using) in 2 tablespoons butter until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Set aside.
In the same skillet, brown the breakfast sausage, breaking it into crumbles. Drain excess grease. Cook bacon until crispy, then crumble. Set meats aside.

Spray a 6-quart crockpot with cooking spray. Layer the hashbrowns on the bottom and sprinkle with Cajun seasoning. Add the sautéed vegetables, cooked sausage, ham, and bacon evenly over the hashbrowns.
In a large bowl, whisk together the scrambled eggs, country gravy, sour cream, heavy cream, hot sauce, black pepper, and paprika. Pour evenly over the meat and hashbrown layers.
Scatter the cubed cream cheese, cheddar cheese, and drained Rotel tomatoes on top. Dot with remaining 2 tablespoons butter.
Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours or high for 3-4 hours, until eggs are fully set and hashbrowns are tender.
Stir gently before serving to combine all the layers. Adjust seasoning with additional hot sauce or black pepper if desired.

d: Indulge in the creamy, cheesy goodness of this Cheeseburger Dip, where ground beef meets a melty blend of Velveeta, cheddar cheese, and cream cheese. The addition of diced onions adds a sweet crunch, making each bite an exciting explosion of flavors. Serve it warm with crispy tortilla chips, and you’ll have a crowd-pleaser that disappears in minutes at any gathering!
i: 6 strips bacon, cooked crispy and crumbled (divided)
1 cup diced onions (divided - half for cooking, half for topping)
dir: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the ground beef with half the diced onions until meat is fully cooked. Drain excess grease.
Reduce heat to medium-low and add the Velveeta, cheddar cheese, cream cheese, and evaporated milk to the skillet. Stir until cheeses are melted and smooth.
Stir in half the crumbled bacon, the pickles, bacon onion jam, burger sauce, and thyme. Mix until well combined and heated through.
Transfer the dip to a serving dish and top with remaining raw onions, diced tomatoes, remaining crispy bacon, and shredded lettuce. Serve hot with tortilla chips, crackers, or toasted bread.

d: Dive into the layers of deliciousness in this Crockpot Vodka Sauce Lasagna, featuring zesty Italian sausage, ricotta cheese, and a rich vodka sauce. As it cooks slowly, the flavors meld beautifully, creating a comforting dish that’s both hearty and satisfying. Perfect for a family dinner, this lasagna is sure to be a showstopper that keeps everyone coming back for seconds!
i: 2 tablespoons fresh basil, chopped (or 1 teaspoon dried)
dir: Brown the Italian sausage in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks. Add onion and garlic during the last 2 minutes. Drain excess fat and stir in vodka sauce.
In a bowl, mix ricotta cheese, egg, 1 cup mozzarella, Parmesan, basil, salt, and pepper until well combined.

Spray your crockpot with cooking spray. Spread a thin layer of meat sauce on the bottom. Break lasagna noodles to fit and layer 3 noodles over sauce. Spread half the ricotta mixture over noodles, then add more meat sauce.
Repeat layers: 3 noodles, remaining ricotta mixture, meat sauce, then final 3 noodles and remaining meat sauce. Pour water around the edges.
Cover and cook on low for 4-5 hours, until noodles are tender. During the last 15 minutes, sprinkle remaining 1 cup mozzarella on top and cover until melted.
Let stand 10-15 minutes before serving so it sets up and slices easier.

d: Crockpot lasagna is a comforting one-pot meal that layers savory ground beef with creamy ricotta cheese and rich marinara sauce. The Italian seasoning and garlic powder elevate the flavors, creating an irresistible aroma as it cooks. This dish combines hearty ingredients that meld together beautifully, making it a perfect, hassle-free dinner that everyone will love!
dir: Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks. Drain excess fat and stir in Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
In a bowl, mix together ricotta cheese, egg, and half the Parmesan cheese until well combined.
Spread a thin layer of marinara sauce on the bottom of your crockpot. Break lasagna noodles to fit and layer them over the sauce.

Spread half the ricotta mixture over noodles, then half the ground beef, half the remaining marinara, and 1/3 of the mozzarella. Repeat layers, ending with noodles, sauce, and remaining mozzarella and Parmesan on top.
Cover and cook on low for 4-5 hours until noodles are tender. Let stand 15 minutes before serving to set up.

d: Indulge in the irresistible flavors of Chicken Enchiladas made in a crockpot, where tender chicken melds with creamy salsa, tangy sour cream, and zesty taco seasoning. The combination of crumbled chorizo and vibrant bell peppers adds a delightful kick, making each bite a fiesta for your taste buds. With the ease of slow cooking, you’ll want to savor this crowd-pleasing dish at every gathering!
dir: In a large bowl, mix together the salsa, cream cheese, sour cream, lime juice, taco seasoning, and fajita seasoning until well combined.
Layer the bottom of a large crockpot with half the tortilla strips, then add the diced chicken, crumbled chorizo, corn, bell peppers, red onion, jalapeños, green chilies, and roasted tomatoes.
